paragraphs: 2001 a space odyssey notes
Quotes I liked:

Behind every man now alive stand thirty ghosts, for that is the ratio by which the dead outnumber the living. Since the dawn of time, roughly a hundred billion human beings have walked the planet Earth.
There are approximately a hundred billion stars in our local universe, the Milky Way.
Though he was still hungry, he was not actually weak with hunger. That was the most of which any man-ape could ever aspire.
They could not eat it, and it could not eat them: therefore it was not important.
The crystal monolith was patient. Neither it, not its replicas scattered across half the globe, expected to succeed with all the scores of groups involved in the experiment.
Though birth control was cheap, reliable, and endorsed by all the main regions, it had come too late. As a result, food was short in every country.
Every time Floyd took off from Earth, he wondered if it would still be there when the time came to return.
Someone had once said that you could be terrified in space, but you could not be worried there. It was perfectly true.
All objects were now six times as sluggish as their mere weight would suggest.

In the 1980s, Minsky and Good had shown how neural networks could be generated automatically - self-replicated - in accordance with an arbitrary learning program. Artificial brains could be grown by a process strikingly analogous to the development of human brain.

Turing had pointed out that, if one could carry out a prolonged conversation with a machine without being able to distinguish between its replies and those that a man might give, then the machine was thinking, by any sensible definition of the word.
The crater looked as if it had been caused by an explosion from inside the ship; at these velocities, materials behaved in strange ways.
“I don’t want to insist on it, Dave, but I am incapable of making an error."
One does not replace a blown fuse - until one knows just why it has blown.
But he took nothing for granted - in space that was a good recipe for suicide.

Bowman felt as if he was in the witness box, being cross-examined by a hostile prosecutor for a crime of which he was unaware - knowing that, although he was innocent, a single slip of the tongue might bring disaster.
“The favourite theory is the simplest, and the most logical. It is also the must disturbing.
You hide a Sun-powered device in darkness - only if you want to know when it Is brought out into the light. In other words, the monolith may be some kind of alarm. And we triggered it."
The dimensions of the monolith were found to be in the exact ration 1 to 4 to 9 - the squares of the first three integers.
Any man, in the right circumstances, could be dehumanised by panic.
Perhaps the creatures who had visited Earth’s Moon so long ago were not merely extraterrestrial, but extrasolar.
Propulsion systems improved out of all recognition, in the end they would meet the impassable barrier of the speed of light.
“What would intelligent extraterrestrials look like?”
They did not believe that really advanced beings would possess organic bodies at all. Mind would eventually free itself from matter.
No one had ever given the slightest thought to the curious coincidence that the rigs of Saturn had been born at the same time as the human race.
In all the galaxy, they had found nothing more precious than Mind, they encouraged its dawning everywhere.
He might have been looking at a photographic negative of the Milky Way. It seemed that space had been turned inside out: this was not a place for Man.
It was some kind of cosmic switching device, routing the traffic of the stars through unimaginable dimensions of space and time. He was passing through a Grand Central Station of the galaxy.
It was as if he were watching sunrise - on a sun.
This must be one of the meeting places for the commerce of the stars.
He was now so close to the red sun that he would have been burned up in a moment if its radiation had not been held at bay by some invisible screen.
The space pod was resting on the polished floor of an elegant, anonymous hotel suite that might have been in any large city on Earth.
It was all a fake, though a fantastically careful one. And it was clearly not intended to deceive but rather - he hoped - to reassure.
A perfectly normal selection from the world’s TV programs. All the programs were about two years old. That was around the time TMA-1 had been discovered.
His host had based their ideas of terrestrial living upon TV programs.
It was merely a toy to distract the senses, while the real processing was carried out at far deeper levels of the mind.

He had returned on time. Down there on that crowded globe, the alarms would be flashing across the radar screens, the great tracking telescopes would be searching the skies - and history as men knew it would be drawing to a close.
For though he was master of the world, he was not quite sure what to do next. But he would think of something.

file: A random walk down wall street notes.html
paragraphs: A random walk down wall street notes
Stuff I underlined:

The message of the original edition was very simple one: Investors would be far better off buying and holding an index fund than attempting to buy and sell individual securities or actively managed mutual funds.
“What is a cynic? A man that knows the price of everything, and the value of nothing” Oscar Wilde

A random walk is one in which future steps or directions cannot be predicted on the basis of past history. When the term is applied to the stock market, it means that short-run changes in stock prices are unpredictable.
Investing is a method of purchasing assets to gain profit in the form of reasonably predictable income (dividends, interest, or rentals) and/or appreciation over the long term.
Just to stay even, your investments have to produce a rate of return equal to inflation.
Investing requires work, but it’s fun.
All investment returns are dependent on future events. That’s what makes the fascination of investing: It’s a gamble whose success depends on an ability to predict the future.

The firm-foundation theory argues that each investment instruments has a firm anchor of something called intrinsic value, which can be determined by careful analysis of present conditions and future prospects. When prices fall below (rise above) this firm foundation of intrinsic value, a buying (selling) opportunity arises, because this fluctuation will eventually be corrected.

The castle-in-the-air theory concentrates on psychic values. Analysing how the crowd of investors is likely to behave in the future and how during periods of optimism they tend to build their hopes into castles in the air, the successful investor tries to beat the gun by estimating what investment situations are most susceptible to public castle-building and then buying before the crowd.

It’s analogous to entering a newspaper beauty judging contest in which one must select the six prettiest faces out of a hundred photographs, with the prize going to the person whose selections most nearly conform to those of the groups as a whole.
The optimal strategy would be to predict what average option is likely to be about what the average opinion will be, and so on.
It’s ok to pay three times what something is worth if later on you can find some innocent to pay five times what it’s worth.
“A thing is worth only what someone else will pay for it."

"October. This is one of the peculiarly dangerous months to speculate in stocks in. The other ones are July, January, September, April, November, May, March, June, December, August and February.” M. Twain
Unsustainable prices may persist for years, but eventually they reverse themselves.
Big losers in the South Sea Bubble included Isaac Newton, who is reported to have said, “I can calculate the motions of heavenly bodes, but not the madness of people”
Selling short is a way to make money if stock prices fall. It involves selling stock you do not currently own in expectation to buying it back later at lower price.

The consistent losers in the market, from my personal experience, are those who are unable to resist being swept up in come kind of tulip-bulb craze. It is not hard to make money in the market. What is hard to avoid is the alluring temptation to throw your money away on short, get-rich-quick speculative binges.
'Everything’s got a moral if only you can find it’ L.Carroll
Buyers of these issues didn’t rally care what the companies made - so long as it sounded electronic, with a suggestion of the esoteric.
You could put together a group of companies with no basic potential at all and produce steadily rising per-share earnings.
The conglomerate had literally manufactured growth. None of the three companies was growing at all; yet simply by virtue of their merger, out conglomerate will show earning growth.
The trick that makes the game work is the ability of electronics company to swap its high-multiple stock for the stock of another company with lower multiple.

It was best to buy stocks with an exciting concept and a compelling and believable story that the market would recognise now - not far in the future. Hence, the concept of the so-called concept stock.
Blue-chip companies were “big capitalization” stocks. These were the stocks that you would never sell. Hence they also were called “one decision” stocks.
No sizeable company could ever grow fast enough to justify an earnings multiple of 80 or 90.
The lessons of market history are clear. Styles and fashions in investors’ evaluations of securities can and often do play a critical role in the pricing of securities.
The promise of the internet spawned the largest creation and largest destruction of stock market wealth of all times.
It was a “positive feedback loops”.
Eventually, one runs out of greater fools.
There was a complete disconnect between stock-market valuations and any reasonable expectations of future growth.
In the first quarter of 2000, 916 venture capital firms invested $15.7 billion in 1009 startups Internet companies. It was as if the stock market was on steroids.
These were not business models. They were models for business failure.
Traditionally, ten stocks were rated “buys” for each one rated “sell”. But during the bubble, the ratio was almost a hundred to one.
In order to justify even higher prices for Internet-related companies, security analysts began to use a variety of “new metrics” that could be used to value the stocks.
In the brave new Internet world, sales, revenue, and profit were irrelevant. Number on people viewing a web page or “visiting” a website was a new metric.
It was the extraordinary New Economy mania that encouraged a string of business scandals that shook the capitalist system to its roots.
Investments in transforming technologies have often proved unrewarding for investors.
The key to investing is not how much an industry will affect society or even how much it will grow, but rather its ability to make and sustain profits.
Under the old system, banks would make mortgages loans and hold those loans until they were repaid. Bankers were very careful.

The system changed and mortgage loans were still made by banks, but were held for only a few days, until they could be sold to an investment banker. The investment banker would then assemble packages of these mortgages and issue mortgage-backed securities.
The credit-default swaps trading in the market grew as much as ten times the value of underlying bonds.
The lender did not need to be as careful, and the standards for making mortgage loans deteriorated sharply.
Fueled by easy credit, house prices began to rise rapidly.
What we know about all bubbles is that eventually they pop.
As home equity collapsed, consumers pulled their horns and went on a spending strike.
The clear conclusion is that the market did correct itself. Eventually, true value is recognized by the market.
The stock market is not a voting mechanism but a weighing mechanism.
Market prices must always be wrong. But at any particular time, it is not obvious to anyone whether they are too high or too low.
No one person or institution consistently knows more than the market.

A coded and password-protected (but anonymous) entry on the ledger records ownership of the bitcoin. The blockchain provides proof of who owns the tokens at any time as well as the payment history of every bitcoin in circulation.

The argument for the disruptive technology involved is that it can allow for seamless and anonymous transactions without the need to go through the banking system and without the use of national currencies.
What is the definition of money? Money is what money does. Money performs three functions in the economy:
It is a medium of exchange.
It is a unit of account, the yardstick that is needed to post prices and record debts now and in the future.
It is a store of value.
Bitcoin meet the first requirements, but the extreme volatility in the value of bitcoin makes it fail the second and third common definitions of money.
There is a central bank whose goal involve maintaining the stability of the value of the currency.
Governments can be expected to crack down on the use of bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies for illegal transactions.
The total network of computers comprising the bitcoin network consumes as much energy each year is some medium-sized countries.
Half of all bitcoin is believe to be held by fewer than 50 holders in 2018. These holder can potentially band together and manipulate the market.
If overnight someone broke the underlying encryption system of the bitcoin protocol, the market could collapse in chaos.
Technical analysis is essentially the making and interpreting of stock charts.
Fundamentalists seek to determine a stock’s proper value.

Why is charting supposed to work? The crowd makes the trend perpetuate themselves, there may be unequal access to fundamental information about the company and investors often under react initially to new information.

Chartists buy only after the price trends have been established, and sells only after they have been broken. Because sharp reversals in the market may occur quite suddenly, the chartist often misses the boat.
If some people know that the price will go to 40 tomorrow, it will go to 40 today.
The fundamentalist strives to be relatively immune to the optimism and pessimism of the crowd.
Take the interest rate you earn and divide it into the number 72, and you get the number of years it will take to double your money.
Some Fundamental analysis rules:
A rational investor should be willing to pay a higher price for a share the larger the growth rate of dividends and earnings.
A rational investor should pay a higher price for a share, other things equal, the larger the proportion of a company’s earnings paid out in cash dividends or used to buy back stock.
A rational investor should pay a higher price for a share, other things equal, the less risky the company’s stock.
A rational investor should pay a higher price for a share, other things equal, the lower the interest rates.
Why fundamental analysis might fail to work?
Information may be incorrect.
Estimate of “value” might be faulty.
The stock price may not converge to its value estimate.
The market might correct its “mistake” by revaluing all stocks downward.
“Things are seldom what they seem. Skim milk masquerades as cream” H.M.S. Pinaforte
Chartists believe momentum exists in the market.
The chart derived from random coin tossings looks remarkably like a normal stock price chart and even appears to display cycles.
Yes, history does tend to repeat itself in the stock market, but in an infinitely surprising variety of ways.
Human nature likes order; people find it hard to accept the notion of randomness. No matter what the laws of chance might tell us, we search for patterns among random events.
It’s sometimes possible to correlate two completely unrelated events. The indicator most closely correlated with the S&P 500 Index is the volume of butter production in Bangladesh.
With large numbers of technicians predicting the market, there will always be some who have called the last turn or even the last few turns, but none will be consistently accurate.
If you examine past stock prices in any given period, you can almost always find some kind of system that would have worked in a given period.
Any regularity in the stock market that can be discovered and acted upon profitably is bound to destroy itself.
Simply buying and holding a diversified portfolio will enable you to save on investments expense, brokerage charges, and taxes.
“How could I have been so mistaken as to have trusted the experts?” John F. Kennedy
Calculations of past earnings growth are no help in predicting future growth.
Analyst can’t predict consistent long-run growth, because it does not exist.
Highly trained and well-paid professionals may not be terribly skilful at their calling. This is hardly unusual. Similar types of findings exists in most groups of professionals.
Five factors that help explain why security analysts have such difficulty in predicting the future:
The influence of random events.
The production of dubious reported earnings through “creative” accounting procedures.
Errors made by analysts themselves.
The loss of the best analysis to the sales desk, to portfolio management, or to hedge funds.
The conflict of interest between research and investment banking departments.
Over long period of time, mutual-fund portfolios have not outperformed the market.
Simply buying and holding the stocks in a broad market inde is a strategy that is very hard for the professional portfolio manager to beat.
Making 100 percent one year and losing 50 percent the next leave you exactly where you started out.
It is the nature of an average that some investors will beat it. With large numbers of investment managers, chance does explain some extraordinary performances.
Index investing is smart investing.
Efficient market hypothesis (EMH):
Weak: looking at past stock prices cannot help investors.
Semi-strong: no public information will help the analyst select undervalued securities.
Strong: nothing that is knowable about a company will benefit the fundamental analyst.
The EMH doesn’t imply that stock prices are always correct. In fact, stock prices are always wrong. What EMH implies is that no one knows for sure if stock prices are too high or too low.
Even Graham came to the conclusion that fundamental security analysis could no longer be counted on to produce superior investments returns.
“Practical men, who believe themselves to be quite exempt from any intellectual influence, are usually the slaves of some defunct economist” J. M. Keynes
Many academics agree that the method of beating the market is not to exercise superior clairvoyance but rather to assume greater risk.
The higher the standard deviation, the more probable it is that at least in some periods you will lose money in the market. That’s why standard deviation is used and justified as indicator of risk.

All investors are risk-averse. They want high returns and guaranteed outcomes. Portfolio of risky stocks might be put together in such a way that the portfolio as a whole could be less risky than the individual stocks in it.

As long as there is some lack of parallelism in the fortunes of the individual companies in the economy, diversification can reduce risk (negative covariance). Diversification will not help much if there is a high covariance (high correlation) between the returns of the two companies.

Negative correlation is not necessary to achieve the risk reduction benefits from diversification. Markowitz’s great contribution to investors’ wallets was his demonstration that anything less than perfect positive correlation can potentially reduce risk.
The paradoxical result of this analysis is that overall portfolio risk is reduced by the addition of a small amount of riskier foreign securities.
“Theories that are right only 50 percent of the time are less economical than coin-flipping” G. J. Stigler
There is no premium for bearing risks that can be diversified away.

Systematic risk arises from the basic variability of stock prices in general and the tendency for all stock to go along with the general market (market risk), unsystematic risk results from factors peculiar to that particular company.

Beta is the numerical description of systematic risk. The beta for any security is essentially the same thing as the covariance between that security and the market index as measured on the basis of past experience.
Systematic risk cannot be eliminated by diversification.
The only part of total risk that investors will get paid for bearing is systematic risk.
Good (sarcastic) idea: buy high-beta stocks when you think that the market is going up, and switch to low-beta ones when you fear that the market might decline.
Anyone can theorise about how security markets work, but does it work?
Does beta alone summarise a security’s total systematic risk?
The relationship between beta and return is essentially flat, but portfolios betas from the past do a reasonably good job of predicting relative volatility in the future.
It is very difficult to measure beta with any degree of precision.
“Behavioural finance is not a branch of standard finance: it is its replacement with a better model of humanity” M. Statman
Many stock-market investors are far from fully rational.
Behavioural finance recognises that people deviate in systematic ways from rationality, and states that it is possible to quantify or classify such irrational behaviour.
There are four factors that create irrational market behaviour:

Overconfidence: tendency to be overconfident about beliefs and abilities and overoptimistic about assessments of the future. People are prone to attribute any good outcome to their own abilities. They tend to rationalise bad outcomes as resulting from unusual external events. Overoptimism in forecasting the growth for exciting companies could then be one explanation for the tendency of “growth” stocks to underperform “value” stocks.
Biased judgements: investors are convinced that they can “control” their investment results.

Herd mentality: groups tend to make better decisions than individuals. “Group thinking”: groups of individuals will sometimes reinforce one another into believing that some incorrect point of view is, in fact, the correct one.
“There is nothing so disturbing to one’s well-being and judgement as to see a friend get rich”.
Loss aversion: prospect theory: people’s choices are motivated by the value they assign to gains and losses. Losses are considered far more undesirable than equivalent gains are desirable.

Pride and regret: investors find it very difficult to admit, even to themselves, that they have made a bad stock-market decision. “Disposition effect”: clear disposition among investors to sell their winning stocks and to hold on ti their losing investments.

Arbitrageurs are expected to take offsetting positions - such as selling overpriced stocks short and buying underpriced ones - so that any misplacing caused by irrational investors is quickly corrected.
The market can remain irrational longer than the arbitrageur can remain solvent.

To sell short, I must borrow the securities to be able to deliver them to the buyer (I must also pay the buyer any dividends that are declared on the stock during the period I hold the short position).
If you seat down at the table and can’t figure out who the sucker is, get up and leave because it’s you.
Most investors beat themselves by engaging in mistaken stock-market strategies rather than accepting the passive buy-and-hold indexing approach recommended.
Avoid stupid investor tricks.
Avoid herd behaviour: invariably, the hottest stocks or funds in one period are the worst performers in the next.
Avoid overtrading: the correct holding period for the stock market is forever.
If you do trade: sell losers, not winners.

Be wary of new issues: Never buy an IPO at prices that are higher than the IPO price. Historically, IPOs have been a bad deal. Poor performance starts about six months after, the period where insiders are prohibited from selling stock to the public.
Stay cool to hot tips: steer clear of any hot tips. Never buy anything from someone who is out of breath.
Distrust foolproof schemes: “Market timing can only be accomplished by liars.”, “If something is too good to be true, it is too good to be true”.
“I’ve gotten a lot of results. I know several thousand things that won’t work.” T. A. Edison

Sharpe ratio: numerator is the excess return over the risk-free rate (e.g. three-month Treasury bill rate), denominator is risk or volatility of the strategy measured by the standard deviation of the results.

Value wins: If they argue that “value” wins over time, but low P/E multiplies and low P/BV(book value) can reflect risk factors that are priced into the market (my note: Dear Malkiel, if you take also into account financial situation and pick only stable companies you don’t have this risk).
Smaller is better: small-company stocks generate larger returns but are riskier.
Single-factor smart beta products have not produced superior results.

RAFI index: capitalisation weighting implies that holders of such portfolios will always be holding too big a share of overpriced growth stocks. It avoids this problem by adjusting the weight of each stock to its economic footprint such as earnings, assets and the like.
Equally-weighted portfolios: Weighting each stock in an index equally, rather than weighting by its total capitalisation.
Smart beta are often testament to smart marketing rather than to smart investing.
The core of every portfolio should consist of low-cost, tax-efficient, broad based index funds.

Ray Dalio developed “risk parity” investment techniques. To increase the return and risk, one can overweight the portfolio with higher risk assets. A second plan is to invest in a broadly diversified portfolio leveraged up to increase both its risk and return (the second is what he’s suggesting).
Dalio’s technique does not rely on active portfolio management.

Leverage is a potentially dangerous tool for investors. The levered investor may be forced to liquidate. Leverage is one technique that needs to be in the investor’s tool box, and it should be judged as being appropriate in some circumstances for investors who hold a broadly diversified portfolio (including International securities) and wish to enhance the entire portfolio’s return and risk with the usage of leverage.
“In investing money, the amount of interest you want should depend on whether you want to eat well or sleep well.” J. K. Morley
The most important driver in the growth of your assets is how much you save, and saving requires discipline.
Trust in time rather than in timing.
The secret of getting rich slowly (but surely) is the miracle of compound interest.
You can only get poor quickly. To get rich, you will have to do it slowly, and you have to start now.
The only thing worse than being dead is to outlive the money you have put aside for retirement.
Everyone needs to keep some reserves in safe and liquid investments.
Remember the overarching rule for achieving financial security: keep it simple.
Short-term investments provide the best rate of return.
Save as much as you can through tax-sheltered means.
Finding you sleeping point is one of the most important investment steps you must take.

How do you felt during a period of sharply declining stock markets? If you became physically ill and even sold out all your stocks rather than staying the course with a diversified investment program, then a heavy exposure to common stocks is not for you.

A good house on good land keeps its value no matter what happens to money. As long as the world’s population continues to grow, the demand for real estate will be among the most dependable inflation hedges. But the real estate market is less efficient than the stock market.
Real estate returns have often exhibited only a moderate correlation with other assets.
Real estate has been a dependable hedge against inflation.

Zero-Coupon Bonds: these securities are purchased at discounts from their face value and gradually rise to their face or par values over the years. If held to maturity, the holder is paid the full stated amount of the bond.
Bond index funds and ETFs just buy and hold a variety of bonds, generally outperform actively managed bond funds.

If interest rates go up, the price of your bonds will go down. But if interest rates go down, the issuer can often “call” the bonds away from you (repay the debt early) and then issue new bonds at lower rates. Make sure that your long-term bonds have a ten-year call-protection provision.
TIPS (Treasury inflation-protected securities) are immune to the erosion of inflation if held to maturity.
Conventional wisdom has usually recommended against bonds from emerging markets.

Collectibles: buy those things because you love them, not because you expect them to appreciate in value. Be aware of fakes and forgeries. You’re going to have insurance premiums and maintenance charges. So you’re making payments instead of receiving dividends or interest.
Trading stocks online is easy and cheap, but few investors who try to trade in and out of stocks each day make profits.
“In the multitude of counsellors there is safety”: whatever the investment objectives, the investor who is wise diversifies.
Firms increasingly prefer distributing their growing earnings to stockholders through stock repurchases rather than dividend increases.
Companies that buy back stocks reduce the number of shares outstanding and increase earning per share and share prices, creating capital gains.
Capital-gain taxes can be deferred until the stocks are sold.
Management compensation is derived from stock options.
Common stocks should be an inflation hedge.
Stocks returns are determined by:
The initial dividend yield
The grow rate of earnings
Changes in valuation in terms of price-earnings
Bond returns are determined by:
The initial yield to maturity
Charges in interest rates
The unexpected frequently happens.
“There are two times in a man’s life when he should not speculate: when he can’t afford it, and when he can."
The most important investment decision you will probably ever make concerns the balancing of asset categories at different stages of your life.
Five asset allocation principles:
Risk and return are related
The longer an investor’s holding period, the lower the likely variation in the asset’s return
Dollar-cost averaging can be useful to reduce the risk
Rebalancing can reduce risk and increase returns
Distinguish between your attitude toward and your capacity for risk

The longer the time period over which you can hold on your investments, the greater should be the share of common stocks in your portfolio. Younger people should have a larger proportion of their assets in stocks than older people.

If you will be building up your investment portfolio slowly over time with the accretion of your yearly savings, you will be taking advantage of dollar-cost averaging. It does help you avoid the risk of putting all your money in the stock or bond market at the wrong time.
Only those who will be sellers of equities in the near future should be happy at seeing stock rise. Prospective purchasers should much prefer sinking prices.

You must have both the car and the confidence to continue making the periodic investments even when the sky is the darkest. No matter how scary the financial news, no matter how difficult it is to see any sign of optimism, you must not interrupt the automatic-pilot nature of the program.
Dollar-cost averaging is not optimal if the market does go straight up.
If possible keep a small reserve to take advantage of market declines and buy a few extra shares if the market is down sharply.

Rebalancing is bringing the proportions of your assets devoted to different assets classes back into the proportions suited to your age and your attitude toward and capacity for risk (no more than once a year).
We don’t have a genie that tell us “buy low and sell high”. Systematic rebalancing is the closes analogue.
Your capacity for risk is related to your age.
Never take on the same risks in your portfolio that attach to your major source of income.
A general rule of thumb is that the proportion of bonds in one’s portfolio should equal one’s age.
We have been a nation of consumers rather than savers.
Boomers have only two realistic choices: begin saving money in a serious way or can beat their odds and die early.
Annuities are contract made with an insurance company where the investor pays a sum of money to guarantee a series of periodic payments that will last as long as the annuitant lives.
At least a partial annuitization usually does make sense.
S&P 500 represents at least three-quarters of the value of all U.S. traded common stocks.
Indexes are tax friendly since they defer the realisation of capital gains. It is also more predictable.
Broad diversification reduce brokerage charges.
ETF are Exchange-traded index funds.
Trade as little as possible.
Selling loss lower your tax bill.
Index should be the core of your portfolio and try the stock-picking game for the money you can afford to put at greater risk.
Tax-loss harvesting involves selling an investment the is trading at a loss and replacing it with a highly correlated but not identical investment.
“Although men flatter themselves with their great actions, they are not so often the result of great design as of chance.”
Timeless lessons involve broad diversification, annual rebalancing, using index funds, and staying the course.
If you will follow the simple rules and timeless lessons espoused in this book, you are likely to do just fine, even during the toughest of times.
Even if the proportion of active managers shrinks to as little as 10 or 5 percent of the total, there would still be more than enough of them to make prices reflect information.
Index funds have no incentive to favour one industry over another.
Index funds have been of enormous benefit for individual investors. Competition has driven the cost to zero. They represent an unambiguous benefit for society.
Other notes:
Really nice plot (pag. 199)

paragraphs: A short history of nearly everything notes
I underlined a lot, I’ll try to write only interesting or funny stuff:

These tiny particles will uncomplainingly engage in all the billions of deft, cooperative efforts necessary to keep you intact and let you experience the supremely agreeable but generally under appreciated state know as existence.
Why atoms take this trouble is a bit of a puzzle.

There is no law that requires the universe to fill itself with small particles of matter or to produce light and gravity and the other physical properties on which our existence hinges. There needn’t actually be a universe at all.
This is a book about how we went from there being nothing at all to there being something, and then how a little of that something turned into us, and also some of what happened in between and since.
Outside the singularity there is no where. When the universe begins to expand, it won’t be spreading out to fill a larger emptiness. The only space that exists is the space it creates as it goes.
Tune your television to any channel it doesn’t receive, and about 1 percent of the dancing static yous see is accounted for by this ancient remnant of the Big Bang.
It seems impossible that you could get something from nothing, but the fact that once there was nothing and now there is a universe is evident proof that you can.
According to Guth’s theory, gravity emerged. And it then was joined by electromagnetism and the strong and weak nuclear forces. Then they were joined by elementary particles.
Some experts believe there may have been many other big bangs, and the reason we exists in this particular one is that this is one we could exists in.
You can never get to the edge of the universe, because the universe bends.
It was named Pluto at least partly because the first two letters made a monogram from Lowell’s initials.
When considering the universe at large we don’t actually know what is in our own solar system.
Just in the Milky Way, the number of advanced civilisations always works out to be somewhere in the millions.
The average distance between any two of these civilisations is reckoned to be at least two hundred light-years.

What would be like if we had four years and four months to watch an inescapable doom advancing toward us, knowing that when it finally arrived it would blow the skin right off out bones? Would people still go to work?
Halley was an exceptional figure. He had a long and productive career. The only thing he didn’t do, interestingly enough, was discover the comet that bears his name.

Using the stuff that makes up your daily life as the vehicle for coming to Union is called karma yoga. It is a most available yoga for all, and at the same time a most difficult one. It is difficult because it starts with an action which initially performing for an end of maintaining your individual ego, and it overrides or converts that motivation into one of service to the higher Self which transcends ego. Bring a third component into every action: if you're digging a ditch, there is you who is digging the ditch, the ditch who is being dug and a third disinterested person (better if enlightened), who is seeing you dig the ditch. The witness is not evaluative, it does not judge your action, it merely notice them.
About bhakti yoga:

The bhakti yoga is the yoga of love and devotion. We are so action oriented that we think of love as something to do, but love has to spring spontaneously form within, it's in no way amenable to any form of inner or outer force.

Song, dance, chanting and prayer have boon throughout the ages traditional forms of bhakti yoga. There are many levels at which you can participate in these rituals (observing, participating, identifying, becoming one). To know that these stages exists does not mean that you can jump ahead of where you are. Whatever the stage you are in, accept it. When you have fully accepted your present degree of participation, only then will you start to experience the next level.
About meditation:

Meditation includes two processes: making the mind concentrated or one-pointed, and bringing to total cessation the turning of the mind. "The human mind is like that monkey, incessantly active by its own nature, then it becomes drunk with the wine of desire, thus increasing its turbulence. After desire takes possession the sting of the scorpion of jealousy at the success of others, and last of all the demon of pride enters the mind, making it think itself of all importance". Only when your mind has become completely calm will you reach enlightenment.
About the rational mind:

Jnana yoga, the path of knowledge arrived at through reasoning and discrimination. Its limitations are that it cannot handle paradoxical or illogical information and that it cannot know that which can only be experienced subjectively. (Yoga means union).

Finally you come to a point where you almost know it all, sixth chakra, but you may well have gotten caught in the last trap: the desire to know it all and still be you, "the knower". You can only be it all, but you can't know it all. The goal is non-dualistic: as long as there is a " knower" and a "known", you are in dualism.
About time and space:
"Where am I?". "Here". "What time is it?". "Now". Say it until you can hear it.
Don't think about the future, just be here now. Don't think about the past, just be here now.
Here and now is enough. You can plan the future in the Here and Now, as long as when the is Now... you're fully Here and Now.
About the course of sadhana:
As you further purify yourself, your impurities will seem grosser and larger. Understand that it's not that you are getting more caught in the illusion, it's just that you are seeing it more clearly.
At some stages you will experience a plateau. Know that once the process has started it doesn't stop; it only appears to stop from where you are looking. Just keep going.
About the zen center:
The fiercest confrontation (with hermitage) is to merely walk into an empty room with your basic survival gear and close the door.
About dying:
Experience you own death. Let your body go, imagine that the life is out of it. Do not speak or move. Imagine that you have died.
Techniques:
For karma yoga and witnessing yourself (pag. 68).
Being mortal notes
Important passages:
I learned about a lot of things in medical school, but mortality wan't one of them. The purpose of medical schooling was to teach how to save lives, not how to tend to their demise.
But death is not a subject that his doctors, friends, or family can countenance.
The chances that he could return to anything like the life ha had even a few weeks earlier were zero. But admitting this and helping him cope with it seemed beyond us.
I knew theoretically that my patients could die, of course, but every actual instance seemed like a violation, as if the rules I thought we were playing by were broken.
Death, of course, is not a failure. Death is normal. I knew these truths abstractly, but I didn't know them concretely.

(Speaking of an Indian guy) One thing he could never get used to was how we treat our old and frail - leaving them to a life alone or isolating them in a series of anonymous facilities, their last conscious moments spent with nurses and doctors who barely knew their names.

We think, nostalgically, that we want the kind of gold age my father had. But the reason we do not have is that, in the end, we do not actually want it. The historical pattern is clear: as soon as people got the resources and opportunity to abandon that way of life, they were gone.
The veneration of elders may be gone, but not because it has been replaced by veneration of youth. It's been replaced by veneration of the independent self.
There remains one problem with this way of living: sooner or later, independence will become impossible.
Why we age is the subject of vigorous debate. The classical view is that aging happens because of random wear and tear. The newest view holds that aging is more orderly and genetically programmed.

We're good at addressing specific, individual problems. Give us a disease, and we can do something about it. But give us an elderly woman with high bloody pressure, arthritic knees, and various other aliments besides and we hardly know what to do and often make matters worse.

It requires each of us to contemplate the unfixables in our life, the decline we will unavoidably face, in order to make the small changes necessary to reshape it. When the prevailing fantasy is that we can be ageless, the geriatrician's uncomfortable demand is that we accept we are not.
Felix knowledge as geriatrician forced him to recognize his decline, but it didn't make it easier to accept.

As you get older, the lordosis of you're tips your head forward. So when you look straight ahead it's like looking up at the ceiling for anyone else. Try to swallow while looking up: you'll choke once in a while.
What could be done to ensure that there are enough geriatricians for the surgering elderly population. "Nothing," he said. "It's too late".

It is not death that the very old tell me they fear. It is what happens short of death - losing their hearing, their memory, their best friends, their way of life. AS Felix put it to me, "Old age is a continuous series of losses.". Philip Roth put it like: "Old age is not a battle. Old age is a massacre".

As fewer of us are struck dead out of the blue, most of us will spend significant periods of our lives too reduced and debilitated to live independently. We do not like to think about this eventuality. As a result, most of us are unprepared for it. We rarely pay more than glancing attention to how we will live when we need help until it's too late to do much about it.
The most common complaint she made is one I've heard often from nursing home residents I've met: "It just isn't home".

Int the twentieth century the function of hospital was mainly custodial, ad if you fell seriously ill doctors tended to you in your bed. From World War II doctor became heroes, and hospitals place of hope and cure.

There is likeness between prison and nursing homes, along with military camps, orphanages and mental hospitals. Places cut of from wider society. All aspect of life conducted int the same place and under the same authority. Daily activities are conducted in large batches. All activities are tightly scheduled. Finally, all the activities has the same plan.
In almost no cases does anyone sit down with you and try to figure out what living a life really means to you under the circumstances.
We find hard to believe that anything better is possible for when we are so weakened and frail that managing without help is no longer feasible. We haven't had the imagination for it.
Living is kind of skill. The calm and wisdom of old age are achieved over time.
How we seek to spend our time may depend on how much time we perceive ourselves to have.

The younger the subjects were, the less they valued time with people they were emotionally close to and the more valued the time with people who were potential sources of information or new friendship. Among the ill, the age differences disappeared. Cultural differences were not significant, either. It's perspective, not age, that matters the most.
The attitude of his sons seemed to result from incomprehension rather than cruelty, but, as Tolstoy would have said, what's the difference in the end?

It's the rare child who is able to think, "Is this place what Mom would want or like or need?" It's more like they're seeing it through their own lens: "Is this a place I would be comfortable leaving Mom?".
I was willing to be rejected. That's what allows you to be a good salesperson.
The Three Plagues of nursing home existence: boredom, loneliness, and helplessness.
The difference in death rates can be traced to the fundamental human need for a reason to live. And is possible to provide them with reasons to live, period.

We all seek a cause beyond ourselves. In ascribing value to the cause and seeing it as worth making sacrifices for, we give our lives meaning. This dedication to a cause beyond oneself is called loyalty. Human beings need loyalty. It does not necessarily produce happiness, and can even be painful.
The best thing your life is when you can go yourself to the bathroom.
Whatever the limits and travails we face, we want to retain the autonomy - the freedom - to be authors of our lives.

The battle of being mortal is the battle to maintain the integrity of one's life - to avoid becoming so diminished or dissipated or subjugated that who you are becomes disconnected from who you were or who you want to be. Sickness and old age make the struggle hard enough. The professionals and institutions we turn to should not make it worse.

The terror of sickness and old age is not merely the terror of the losses one is forced to endure but also the terror of isolation. They ask only to be permitted to keep shaping the story of their life in the world - to make choices and sustain connections to others according to their own priorities.

In the United States, 25 percent of all Medicare spending is for the 5 percent of patients who are in their final year of life, and most of that money goes for care in the last couple of months that is of little apparent benefit. (Data from elsewhere are similar)
Almost all these patients had known, for some time, that they had a terminal condition. Yet they - along with their families and doctors - were unprepared for the final stage.

People with serious illness have priorities besides simply prolonging their lives. Top concerns include avoid suffering, strengthening relationship with family and friends, being mentally aware, not being a burden to others, and achieving a sense that their life is complete.
Last words hardly seem to exist anymore.

The difference between standard medical care and hospice is not the difference between treating and doing nothing. The difference is in priorities. In ordinal medicine, the goal is to extend life. Hospice help people with a fatal illness have the fullest possible lives right now.
Hospice has tried to offer a new ideal for how we die.

The people who opts for these treatments aren't thinking about getting a few added months. They're thinking years. They're thinking they're getting at least that lottery's ticket's chance that their disease might not even be a problem anymore.
People who had substantive discussion with their doctor about their end-of-life preferences are far more likely to die at peace and in control of their situation and to spare their family anguish.
Those who saw a palliative care specialist stopped chemotherapy sooner, entered hospice far earlier, experiencing less suffering at the end of their lives - and they lived 25 percent longer.
You live longer only when you stop trying to live longer.
"Just ask patient what they want when they're conscious".
Death is the enemy. But enemy has superior forces. Eventually, it wins. And in a war that you cannot win, you don't want a general who fights to the point of total annihilation.
Three stages of medical development:
In extreme poverty most deaths occur in the home because people don't have access to professional diagnosis and treatment.
In developing countries, people turn to health care systems when they are ill. They often die in the hospital.
In advanced countries, people have means to become concerned about the quality of their lives, even in sickness, and deaths at home actually rise again.
Different kind of relationship from clinicians and patients:
Paternalistic: ensure that patients receive what we believe best for them.
Informative: we tell facts and figures. The rest is up to you.
Interpretative (what people desire): give information, control but also guidance. Help patients determine what they want.
The closing phase of a modern life often looks like - a mounting series of crises from which medicine can offer only a brief and temporary rescue.
We witnessed for ourselves the consequences of living for the best possible day today instead of sacrificing time now for time later.

What is courage? Courage is strength in the face of knowledge of what is to be feared or hoped. Wisdom is prudent strength. At least two kind of courage are required in aging and sickness: courage to confront the reality of mortality and the courage to act on the truth we find.

The ratings in term of pain in an clinical operation follow the "Peak-End rule", instead of the sum moment-by-moment, that is an average of the pain experienced at the single worst moment of the procedure and the very end.
For human beings, life is meaningful because is a story. A story has a sense as a whole, and its arc is determined by the significant moments, the ones where something happens.

People want to share memories, pass on wisdom and keepsakes, settle relationships, establish their legacies, make peace with God, and ensure that those who are left behind will be okay. They want to end their stories on their own terms.
We think our job is to ensure health and survival. But really it is larger than that. It is to enable well-being.
To read:
How to talk to someone who's dying: pag. 225
Blindness notes
I didn’t underlined much, but really good book:
I am blind.
They say that blindness is black, well I see everything white.
If it's true that the opportunity does not always make the thief, it is also true that it helps a lot.
This is the stuff we’re made of, half indifference and half malice.
The doctor’s wife felt as if she were behind a microscope and observing the behaviour of a number of human beings who did not even suspect her presence.
They have scarcely spoken, their present unhappiness outweighs their past love.
No one could know, at the outset, whether there would be enough food for everyone.
People get so used to having eyes that they think they can use them when they no longer serve for anything.
In the country of the blind, the one-eyed man is king.
The problem of these blind internees could only be resolved by physically wiping out the lot of them, just as one amputates a gangrenous limb in order to save the rest of the body.

A colonel here who believes the solution would be to shoot the blind as soon as they appear. Now that he has gone blind, it’ll be interesting to see what he thinks of that bright idea of his now. He shot himself in the head, Now that’s what I call a consistent attitude.
If we cannot live entirely as human beings, at least let us do everything in our power not to live entirely like animals.
Fear can cause blindness.
Don’t think that blindness has made us better people, It hasn’t made us any worse, We’re on our way though.
He who pays in advance always ends up being badly served.
How did they recognise each other, good heavens, by their voices, of course, it is not only the voice of blood that needs no eyes, love, which people say is blind, also has a voice of its own.
Then she, as she had always done, took him by one arm, bu the gesture now had another meaning, never had he so badly needed someone to guide him as this moment.
Sense of smell, the most delicate of the senses. The worst thing about trying to live a reasonable life in hell is getting used to the dreadful stench down there.
The smell of vomit is only noticed when the atmosphere and all the rest does not smell the same.
The worst thing of all is that I might feel some pleasure.
For each day that we’re deprived of food because of you, one of the men here will die the moment he steps outside this door.
And when is necessary to kill? When what is still alive is already dead.
Just as the habit does not make the monk, the sceptre does not make the king.
Blindness is also this, to live in a world where all hope is gone.
We are so used to the convenience of piped water bought into our homes.
How fragile life is when it is abandoned.
Today is today, tomorrow will bring what tomorrow brings, today is my responsibility, not tomorrow if I should turn blind.
I’m convinced the entire population is blind, there is no water, there is no electricity, there are no supplies of any kind, this must be what chaos is, this is what is really meant by chaos.
Perhaps humanity will manage to live without eyes, but then it will cease to be humanity.
Withdraw, take myself off, disappear, as elephants used to do.
Another saying no longer much used, what eyes do not see the heart does not grieve over.
Old people cannot do much but their work is not to be despised.
Keep what is of no use at the moment, and later you will find what you need.
Illness may differ from one person to another but what is really killing us now is blindness.
The difficult thing isn’t living with other people, it’s understanding them.
Silence is the best applause.
It even used to be said that there is no such thing as blindness, only blind people, when the experience of time had taught us nothing other than that there are no blind people, but only blindness.
I don’t think we did go blind, I think we are blind, Blind but seeing, Blind people who can see, but do not see.
