BIA Techniques
Bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) is a noninvasive, relatively inexpensive method for measuring body composition.

BIA works via measurement of the amount of impedance or resistance to a small, painless electrical current passed through the body between two electrodes, which are often placed on the wrist and ankle.

Total body water (TBW) is estimated from the impedance measurement because electrolytes in the body's water are excellent conductors of electrical current. Impedance measures are higher in individuals with large amounts of body fat because of the low water content in adipose tissue. Conversely, individuals with larger amounts of fat free mass (FFM) have less resistance to the current flowing through their bodies because the water content of FFM is relatively large (-73% water).
Some authors have suggested that BIA methods for determining body composition are roughly as accurate as skinfold techniques.

Inexpensive lower body (foot-to-foot) and upper body (hand-to-hand) BIA devices have become available for home and commercial use. They provide estimates of %BF and FFM using proprietary equations developed by the manufacturers.
For healthy clients with normal fluid balance, these analyzers provide reasonably accurate estimates of FFM, reporting small prediction errors.

BIA measurements can be easily and significantly affected by factors such as hydration status, racial characteristics, and the prediction equation used. Eating, drinking, dehydration, exercise, and men- strual cycle phase can affect total body resistance and the estimate of FFM.
There is a tendency for BIA to overestimate body fat in lean individuals and underestimate body fat in obese individuals.
BIA pretesting guidelines:
Refrain from eating or drinking within four hours of the test
No exercise within 12 hours of the test
No alcohol consumption within 48 hours of the test
No diuretic medications within seven days of the test
Do not test female clients who perceive they are retaining water during their menstrual cycle
Ask clients to void their bladder within 30 minutes of the test.

The personal trainer can use submaximal cardiovascular endurance tests to attain a reasonably accurate estimation of a client's v02max. Submaximal exercise tests are used most often because of high equip- mentexpenses, the personnel needed, and the increased risks associated with maximal tests.

The concept behind a submaximal test is to monitor HR, BP, or rating of perceived exertion (RPE)-or some combination of these-during exercise until a predetermined percentage of the client's predicted maximal HR is achieved, at which point the test is terminated.
Maximal tests are not safe or necessary for many clients and sometimes cannot be conducted without physician supervision.
Assumptions and Solutions for Submaximal Exercise Tests
Assumption 1: Heart rate measurements must be steady state.

Solution: personal trainers should record HR values at the end of a constant work- rate stage or after 2 or 3 minutes of exercise at a constant work rate (6). Steady-state HR is defined as two consecutive HR measurements that are within five beats/min of each other
Assumption 2: True maximal HR for a given age must be the same for all clients.
Solution: the typical equation to calculate age-predicted maximal HR can introduce an unknown error into the model for submaximal estimation of v02max.
Assumption 3: The relationship between HR and work rate must be strong, positive, and linear
Solution: The positive relationship between HR and workload is most linear between 50% and 90% of maximal HR.
Assumption 4: Mechanical efficiency (VO2 at a given work rate) is the same for all clients
Solution: Personal trainers should choose a test that is specific to the client's existing cardiovascular exercise mode(s), daily activities, or both.

Chapter 12 - Flexibilitv and Warm-Up Concepts and Bodvweight and Stability Ball Exercise Technique

There can be confusion about the notion that people must achieve extreme levels of flexibility to reduce the chance of injury and to improve movement capabilities. This does not accurately represent the role that flexibility plays in training.
Flexibility is an important piece of the training puzzle; but like other aspects of training it must be based on the needs of the individual.
According to a common definition, flexibility is the range of motion of a joint or a series of joints.
For personal trainers, a more relevant definition might be the ability of a joint to move freely through the full normal range of motion (ROM).
Every workout should be preceded by a warm-up session. However, the ideal time to perform flexibility training is dependent on the nature of the activity that is to take place during the workout.

Achieving optimal flexibility helps improve movement efficiency by allowing joints to move freely through a full normal ROM, and it also reduces the risk of musculoskeletal injuries; prevents the development of muscular imbalances; and improves posture, strength, range of motion, and power.
Improving flexibility is a fundamental element of any training program.

Because of these important benefits, it is recommended that personal trainers supervise stretching just as they would any other part of the training session. Doing this communicates the importance of the warm-up and stretching period and may encourage clients to prioritize this portion of the training session.
Flexibility training is important because of the role that flexibility plays in improving movement performance and reducing the opportunity for injury.
Factors Affecting Flexibility
Joint Structure
Joint structures vary between individuals, and the personal trainer must consider this variation when evaluating flexibility.
Joint structure also varies between joints. Some joints offer a reduced ROM compared with others by virtue of their construction.
It is incorrect to think that a single flexibility test can provide an accurate measure of overall flexibility.
Muscle and Connective Tissue

Connective tissue (muscles, ligaments, and tendons is the area of emphasis during ROM exercise. This is because, under normal circumstances, connective tissues are the major structures limiting joint ROM.

Most of the differences between individuals in static ROM are due to the elastic properties of the muscle and tendons attached across the joints. "Stiff” muscles and tendons reduce ROM, while "compliant" muscles and tendons increase ROM. It is these elastic properties that are altered from stretching exercises.

When a muscle is held at a fixed length while under tension in a static stretch, the passive tension [i.e., the amount of external force required to lengthen the relaxed muscle] declines. (Effect lasting up to 20 mins).
Hyperlaxity
Hyperlaxity allows the joints of the body to achieve a ROM that exceeds what is considered normal.

If it has been determined that a client has joint hyperlaxity, the personal trainer should use caution when implementing a stretching program and should ensure that the client has been assessed by an appropriate health care professional.
Age
The biological age of an individual can have a significant impact on flexibility.
Although flexibility tends to diminish as one ages, this reduction may be partially attributable to a decrease in overall physical activity throughout the life span.
However, a well-designed flexibility training program is effective for increasing joint ROM among older adults.
Sex

Sex may also have a significant impact on flexibility levels. It is well known that the connective tissues of men and women differ physiologically, although the mechanisms contributing to these differences are not well understood.
After accounting for body weight, body mass, and limb size, sex-related differences in musculotendinous stiffness are incon- sequential.
Temperature
ROM is positively affected by an increase in either core temperature or external temperature.
The positive effect of increased core temperature on ROM points to the importance of warming up before participating in flexibility training.
Activity Level
As would be expected, people who are physically active tend to be more flexible than inactive individuals.
The decrease in flexibility in inactive individuals primarily occurs because connective tissues may become less pliable when exposed only to limited ROMs.
Resistance Training
A well-designed and properly executed resistance training program using exercises that are performed through a full range of motion can also increase flexibility.
All exercises should be performed through the full available ROM of the involved joints.

Although improper resistance training can impair flexibility, the reason is not usually that the person has become too muscular, or “muscle bound.” Instead the decrease occurs because of the improper development of a muscle or a group of muscles around a joint, resulting in a restriction of motion at that joint.

Flexibility is influenced by a variety of factors. Some of these factors (e.g., joint structure, age, and sex) cannot be influenced by training. However, core temperature during flexibility training, overall activity level, participation in a well-designed resistance training program, and stretching on a regular basis can all affect flexibility and can be positively influenced by the personal trainer.
Flexibility training targets two different tissue adaptations: elasticity and plasticity.
Elasticity refers to the ability to return to original resting length after a passive stretch. Thus, elasticity provides a temporary change in length.
In contrast, plasticity refers to the tendency to assume a new and greater length after a passive stretch, even after the load is removed

Ligaments and tendons have both plastic and elastic properties. When connective tissue is stretched, some of the elongation occurs in the elastic tissue elements and some occurs in the plastic elements.
The specific stretching techniques used by the personal trainer should be designed to produce a plastic elongation if a permanent increase in ROM is the goal.

Active stretching occurs when the person who is stretching supplies the force of the stretch. In contrast, passive stretching occurs when a partner or stretching device provides the force for the stretch
Types of Flexibility Training
Ballistic Stretching
Ballistic stretching involves continuous, rapid bouncing movements at the end ROM where the muscle is at maximal length.

It is generally no longer considered an acceptable method for increasing ROM because there is an increased risk of injury to the muscles and connective tissues associated with these types of movements, especially in joints where there has been a previous injury.
Disadvantages:
Increased danger of exceeding the extensibility limits of tissues involved.
Greater energy requirement.
Activation of the stretch reflex.
The stretch reflex occurs in response to the extent and rapidity of a muscle stretch.
It causes contraction of the previously stretched extrafusal muscle fibers (to protect themselves from overstretching).
Static Stretching
The most used method of increasing flexibility is static stretching.
A slow, constant speed is used. with the stretched position held for approximately 30 seconds.
Static stretching involves relaxation and simultaneous lengthening of the stretched muscle.
Static stretching does not activate the stretch reflex of the muscle.
There are no real disadvantages to static stretching in terms of injury potential if proper technique is used.

Individuals beginning a flexibility program may find it challenging to hold a stretched position for longer durations. Therefore. the personal trainer may initially decrease the duration of the stretch and progress to longer time intervals as tolerance improves.

To prevent activation of the stretch reflex, the client should move into the final static stretch position slowly and only to a point of minor discomfort. As the stretched position is held, the feeling of tension should diminish: if it does not, the stretched position should be slightly reduced.
Recommendations for Static Stretching
Stretching should be preceded by a warm-up of 5 to 15 minutes, until a light sweat appears.
Emphasize slow, smooth movements and coordinate deep breathing.
Properly performed stretches should cause no more than mild discomfort. lf clients feel pain, they are stretching too far.
Ensure that clients do not lock their joints.
To reduce the chance of activating the stretch-reflex, discourage bouncing.
Large muscle groups should be stretched first, and the same routine should be repeated every training day.
Stretches should be done at least three times per week and, to track performance improvements, should be done at the same time of day.
The ideal time to stretch is after aerobic activity or resistance training, when core temperature is maximally elevated.
Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation
It has since expanded to the conditioning of both athletes and the general population as a method of increasing ROM.

There are a variety of PNF techniques, but perhaps the most common method (i.e., the hold- relax method) involves taking the muscle or join into a static stretch position while keeping the muscle relaxed. After this static stretch position is held for about 10 seconds. the muscle is contracted for 6 seconds with a strong isometric contraction against an external fixed object (i.e., a force acting in the direction of the stretch).
After a very brief (1-2 second) rest. another passive stretch is performed for 30 seconds, potentially resulting in a greater stretch.
Because a partner is needed, PNF can be more time consuming than other methods, and the partner must be careful not to overstretch the muscle.
Practically, though, PNF methods are not generally needed.
Dynamic Stretching
Dynamic stretching avoids bouncing and includes movements specific to a sport or movement pattern.

An example of a dynamic stretch is a lunge walk in which the client exaggerates the length of the stride and flexes the back leg so that he or she ends up in a position in which the front knee is over the toe (but not in front of it) and the back knee is just off the flor.
Dynamic stretching emphasizes functionally based movements.

Personal trainers who wish to implement dynamic flexibility training in a client's program should begin dynamic stretches with low volume and low intensity because dynamic flexibility exercises require balance and coordination.
Many of the guidelines established for static flexibility training programs are also applicable to dynamic flexibility training.

There are two primary advantages of combining movements. First, the variety is greater, so the program is less likely to become monotonous. Second, combining stretches is more time efficient because the client is stretching a larger number of muscle groups rather than duplicating the same stretch repeatedly.
The number and types of dynamic stretches that can be used is limited only by the creativity of those designing the programs.

Dynamic and PNF stretching may be the most appropriate types of flexibilitv training for improving movement capability before a workout. If additional flexibilitv work is needed, performance of static flexibilitv exercises after the workout is effective.
Recommendations for Dynamic Stretching
Moderation and common sense are important.
Flexibility is just one component of fitness and should not be overemphasized
The stretch should never be forced. If the stretch hurts, it should be discontinued.
Flexibility training should be combined with resistance training.
Flexibilitv should be joint specific based on the needs of the client and the requirements of the activity.
Ballistic stretching should be avoided.

Stretching movements that position the body in the most functional stance possible, relative to the involved joints and musculature to be stretched and the activity requirements of the client, should be emphasized.
It is important to make use of gravity, body weight and ground reaction forces when stretching.

The dynamic flexibility training program should be specific to the demands of the sport or activities the client takes part in. The individual flexibility requirements of the client are also an important consideration.
Improvements in flexibility can occur from day to day.
Additionally, once increases in ROM have occurred, it is easy to maintain that ROM. Maintaining flexibility requires less work than improving it does.
Clients should stretch the large muscle groups first and repeat the same routine every training day.
As areas that are less flexible become apparent, a greater emphasis can be placed on performing additional stretches for those muscle groups and joints.

Train for dynamic flexibility at least three times per week or along with each exercise session. To track performance improvements, clients should be consistent with the time of day they perform dynamic flexibility training, remem- bering they are least flexible in the morning
Stretching should take place after the core temperature has been elevated.
A combination of dynamic and static flexibility training is recommended when the goal of training is increased ROM.
Warm-up is an activity that raises the total body temperature, as well as temperature of the muscles to prepare the body for vigorous exercise.

Warming up is a part of the foundation of a successful practice session. Getting fully warmed up, mentally and physically, is a key aspect of attaining the training intensity required to achieve optimal results.
Unfortunately many clients attempt to take shortcuts in the warm-up procedure, which may translate into poor performance and increased injury risks.

Flexibility exercises should not be used as the sole method of warming up. Instead, they should be performed after core temperature has been elevated to a point that the client is beginning to perspire.
Types of Warm-Up
Passive Warm-Up
Passive warm-up involves such methods as hot showers, heating pads, or massage.
One obvious advantage of a passive warm-up is that it does not fatigue a client before an exercise session.
Unfortunately, passive warm-up procedures (.g., a moist heat pack) may not be practical in many settings.
General Warm-Up
A general warm-up consists of basic activities requiring movement of the major muscle group.
Specific Warm-Up

Unlike general warm-up, specific warm-up includes movements that are an actual part of the activity, such as slow jogging before going out on a run or lifting lighter loads in the bench press exercise before progressing to the workout weight. A specific warm-up appears to be the most desirable method because it increases the temperature of the same muscles that will be used in subsequent, more strenuous activity and may also serve as a mental rehearsal of the event, allowing complex skills to be performed more effectively
RAMP Warm-up
The RAMP warm-up is a systematic method of pre- paring the body for more vigorous activity. It consists of three main phases: raise. activate and mobilize and potentiation.
Warm-Up Guidelines
The amount, intensity, and duration of the warm-up should ideally be adjusted to every individual depend- ing on his or her level of fitness.
In general, the warm-up activity should last approximately 5 to 15 minutes, long enough for the individual to break into a light sweat.
As conditioning improves, the intensity and duration of the warm-up need to increase.
The warm-up should not create significant fatigue.
Bodyweight training

Bodyweight training is simply a mode of resistance training in which the resistance is provided by the body rather than by an external weight such as a barbell or the weight stack of a selectorized machine In cases in which no equipment is available or if the client prefers this type of training, bodyweight training is a viable option.

The personal trainer needs to be aware that clients will not develop maximal strength or power with bodyweight training because it cannot provide the intensity necessary to develop these physiological adaptations.
Emphasis must be on performing each exercise in a slow, controlled manner with perfect technique.
Suspension Training
Suspension training describes a specific type of bodyweight training that uses adjustable straps suspended from an overhead anchor point.

First, it allows the client to overload specific muscle groups and exercises, and second, it allows for a range of intensities that may be difficult to accomplish via traditional calisthenic bodyweight training.
The degree of resistance varies depending on the individual's center of mass in relation to the anchor point.
The intensity of many upper body pulling exer- cises, such as a suspension row, increases when using a single-arm variation.
Like other forms of body weight exercise, the total volume load for suspension training is difficult to quantify.

For this reason, suspension training may not be the most appropriate form of training for all training goals and all situations because stronger individuals may have a difficult time overloading the targeted musculature using this modality. However, the addition of other devices, such as weighted vests. can safely increase the training load of many suspen- training exercises
The degree of resistance when performing a suspension training exercise varies depending on the individual's center of mass in relation to the anchor point.
Recommendations for Suspension Training:
Securely anchor the suspension training system to a stable object.
Adjust the length of the straps based on the exercise and desired intensity level.
After adjusting the strap length, the personal trainer should make sure the straps are even in length.
Make certain the handles and foot cradles are secured and do not slip when load (i.e., the client's body mass) is applied.
Make certain the client has a firm, closed grip of the suspension trainer handles when using the straps for support.
Ensure the feet are securely in the foot cradles before the client begins exercises aimed at developing the legs or trunk.

When performing suspension training exercises that involve holding onto the handles: To increase the difficulty, clients lower the body closer to the floor by stepping toward the anchor point To decrease the difficulty, clients step away from the anchor point.

To emphasize balance and stability, the foot position can be made narrower (i.e., feet together to hip width). To increase stability and force production, the base should be wider (i.e. hip to shoulder width)
Allow time for the client to become familiar with each suspension trainer exercise.
Emphasize correct technique, which will limit client fatigue.
Manual Resistance Training

Manual resistance training involves the application of an external resistance, applied by a partner or personal trainer via manual muscle force, through a full or partial range of motion for an exercise.
It allows a personal trainer to use an accommodating, rather than a constant, resistance throughout the full range of an exercise.
Manual resistance training can be a viable method of developing muscular fitness if the acute training variables of resistance training (i.e., intensitv. volume. and rest) are appropriately applied.
Recommendations for Manual Resistance Training:
For manual resistance exercises that require the personal trainer to lay hands on the client, the client should be informed beforehand about the procedures and provide consent.
Check for damage to any equipment being used to apply manual resistance to make certain it does not create a safety risk.
When applying manual resistance, adjust the training load based on the number of goal repetitions to achieve the desired muscular adap- fation.
The amount of resistance applied should be consistent throughout the entire range of motion for the exercise selected.
In general, applying resistance to the distal end of a seament is more challenging than when this resistance is applied more proximal
Clients should maintain correct form throughout the entire exercise movement.
Stability Ball Training

The primary motivation for the use of stability balls in these applications is the belief that an unstable surface will provide a greater challenge to the trunk muscles. increase dynamic balance, and possibly help stabilize the spine to prevent injuries.

Stability balls and core training

Personal trainers might choose to incorporate instability into training programs via methods other than stability ball training. Two such methods are described here:
Emphasis on structural multijoint exercises (e.g. squats and deadlifts)
Instability with free-weight training. Free-weight training can provide a moderate degree of instability.
Another way to augment instability in free-weight training is to emphasize unilateral over bilateral dumbbell training.
It is important that people start off with basic, less complex exercises and increase the complexity over time.
People with long hair should tie it back so it does not get caught during movements.
If an exercise causes pain, the personal trainer should modify the movement or the movement should be discontinued.
Making sure the ball is correctly sized. The individual should sit on the ball: the size is correct if the thighs are slightly above parallel to the floor.

One investigation showed a significant increase in abdominal muscle activity when a crunch was performed on a stability ball in comparison to the same movement performed on the floor, but only when the ball was correctly placed.
Guidelines for Stability Ball Training
The stability ball should be fully inflated so that it is firm.

The stability ball should be the correct size for the client. To determine the correct size. have the client sit on the ball with feet on the floor. In this position the thighs should be parallel or slightly above parallel to the floor.
As with other modes of training, a warm-up session of 5 to 15 minutes should precede the actual workout.
Allow time for the client to become familiar with the ball (especially if they train mostly with machines).
Emphasize correct technique. Attention to detail is critical when clients perform exercises on a stability ball.
The number of sets and repetitions performed will depend on the fitness level of the client.

Pause between sentences
Don’t talk like a valley girl
Sit in the from two-thirds of the chair

This book can help you communicate your message, your talent, your ambitions, your goals, your perceived contribution to your community, to those around you. And to do it simply and clearly.
SPEAKING

If we want to improve our ability to connect with others, to understand them and to be understood more clearly, the easiest and most effective way to do so is to focus less on ourselves and more on the other person.
Instead of thinking, "What am I trying to convey?" we should ask ourselves, "Why is he reading my email or attending this meeting? What does she hope to get out of this presentation?"
News flash: your audience don't care about you. They don't really care about your content. They care about how your content impacts them.
Being helpful to the audience is the only legitimate reason for sharing the information.
TIPS FOR CLEAR MESSAGE
Whenever you are participating in a discussion with clients or colleagues, craft a clear message. A clear message:

Is short: key message limited to one sentence, preferably fewer than 10 words long. Consider breaking the content into smaller sentences to help your listeners. Ask: "Will my audience be able to repeat this message to someone else after this meeting?"
Use simple language: big words do not impress anyone. Big ideas do. In a professional setting, you're not graded on smarts. People assume you are smart. You're graded on having impact.
Avoid jargon.
Is focused on the needs of audience: Ask: "What does this audience need to learn by attending this meeting?". Do not focus on your content, but how his audience needs to use your content.

Always stay positive. Turn the conversation back to the other person. If you're talking, you're not learning. Make small talks. If you've heard your voice and not his for more than two minutes, it's time to ask the other person a question.

Instead of seeing ourselves based on our status, we view ourselves from the perspective of how we impact other people. (Real Estate Attorney vs Help Build Housing). It's all about being relevant to the other person.
He remember the teaching point from the program because of the story, and he remembered the story because stories stick with us.
Stories should sound unrehearsed. But it's important to know how you're going to start and how you're going to finish.
A good story:
Begin with a time or place that establishes context
The middle of the story should explain the struggle and build tension
End with a point, that should be clear
When people listen to you, they want to know that they are getting the genuine you.
Using humor in a presentation is like the price of a diamond: if you have to ask, you can't afford it.
If you are going to tell a funny story do not make fun of other people, buy you can poke fun at yourself, lightly.
There are no points lost because you're not funny, but you lose ground if you try to be funny and fail.
Keep focus on the other person even when organising your information.
Start with the broadest possible assessment of the situation and then dive in. Giving away control may seem scary, but it's the most effective way to convey information.
When you're giving a presentation, avoid using the word "presentation". No one wants to be "presented to", use "talk about" instead.
Avoid using the word "slide". Don't talk about the medium. Talk about the content.
When you talk to a larger audience, you either want the to know something (informative format) or you want the to do something (persuasive format).
Informative roadmap:
Context or Hook (problem, fact or statistic, dramatic image)
Agenda (topic A, topic B, topic C)
Topic A (fact or statistic, example or image, story)
Topic B (fact or statistic, example or image, story)
Topic C (fact or statistic, example or image, story)
Summary (topic A, topic B, topic C)
Next Steps (who? what? when?)
Basically:
Tell them what you're going to tell them
Tell them what you've got
Tell them what you've just told them
The repetition drive home the key ideas.
Persuasive presentation format:
Context or Hook (problem, fact or statistic, dramatic image)
Recommendation (brief, specific, memorable)
Benefits (time, feelings, money)
Prove benefit #1 (fact or statistic, example or image, story)
Prove benefit #2 (fact or statistic, example or image, story)
Prove benefit #3 (fact or statistic, example or image, story)
Summary (recommendation, benefits)
Next Steps (who? what? when?)
The gist of the persuasive format is to mention very briefly what you want, and then to spend the majority of your talk telling your audience why they should want it.
When I'm listening to a business presentation, I want to know what I'm supposed to do with this information (personal note: all-hands/demo problem).

The hook: state at the beginning and position this problem as the single most important issue you need to solve as a group. Ask rhetorical questions: it allows you to frame the discussion and creates the illusion of participation.
Use statistics, you can make statistics reflect whatever you want.

If the speaker feels that he is in a one-on-one conversation, he automatically relaxes and has a more conversational tone. Asking a rhetorical question and only looking at one person you trick your brain into thinking that you're in a private conversation with that one person.
Don't build your case toward a conclusion. The audience hears any details you share in context if you start by telling them where they are headed.

It's not just convincing enough to just tell audiences how your recommendation benefits them. You need to prove that. That means showing how it is real by referencing something outside your own opinion. A testimonial, a statistic or an anecdote.
Next steps: who will do what by when. This create a sense of accountability.
How to create the content: write your benefit, your recommendation, go back and create your hook and then procede with proving your benefits.
There is no "wrong" way to communicate. Instead, there is a "spectrum of effectiveness" from less effective to more effective.

When you scan the audience, your brain takes in too much information, your body kicks into a defense mechanism called "fight or flight". You hearth rate increases to pump the blood to your hands so you can fight and your feet so you can flee.

Look at one person at a time for the complete sentence. You'll relax (you're not afraid of speaking to one person), you'll avoid distraction, you build rapport with your audience (talking to everyone, you're not really talking to anyone), you look more composed, you sound more confident and comfortable with yourself.
If you know there is one decision-maker, give that person more attention but don't ignore the others.

Even in one-on-one, maximise eye contact. Don't stare, break eye contact dozens of times. You should be conscious about keeping eye contact. Don't talk during eye contact breaks, you'll look evasive or insecure.

If you speak too quickly in front of an audience, you will sound as if you are apologizing for taking up their time. You'll diminish your presence and your appearance of confidence. (If you talk to one person at a time, you'll automatically slow down your rate of speech).
Two factors can cause the audience to become overwhelmed be a speaker's pace:
The speed of the speaker's voice
The absence of pauses between sentences
Always speak at the volume needed to reach the person farthest to you, even when you're watching the closest to you.
When you smile genuinely, your voice automatically sounds more positive, has more energy, and you'll sound more optimistic.

"Valley girl": speaker's voice inflects "up" at the end of the sentence as if the person were asking a question. Don't do that, it's hard to convey a sense of confidence in this case. Advice and guidance should sound like a statement, not a question.
Your goal with your body language is to minimize the audience's ability yo misperceive you.
If you sit in the front two-thirds of the chair, it's almost impossible to start swiveling, and you are more likely to sit up straight. Try to keep your spine perfectly vertical.

Steel
Metals are made of crystals. A razor gets blunt because the many collisions with hairs that it encounters force bits of these crystals to rearrange themselves into a different shape.

Viewed through an electron microscope, inside of crystals there are squiggly lines - these are dislocations. They are defect in the metal crystals. When you bend a paper clip, it is in fact the metal crystals that are bending.

Alloys tend to be stronger than pure metals because alloy atoms have a different size and chemistry from the host metal's atom, so when they sit inside the host crystal they cause all sorts of mechanical and electrical disturbances that make it more difficult for dislocations to move.

The samurai innovations consisted in separating the different types of steel, so that they could make sure that the low-carbon steel was used to make the center of the sword. This gave the sword an enormous toughness. On the edge of the blade they welded the high-carbon steel, which was brittle but extremely hard and could therefore be made very sharp.

Revolution to mass-production: rather than trying to remove the carbon until just the right amount was left, about 1 percent, Mushet suggested removing all the carbon and then adding 1 percent carbon back in.

Brearley saw a bright glimmer in the pile of rusting specimens. The addition of chromium had not made the steel harder, hence he had rejected the sample, but it had done something much more interesting (stainless steel).
Paper
Paper is a mound of tiny fibers that resembles a bale of hay.
Books en masse are more than a library, they are a statement of identity.

The genius of this so-called codex format - a stack of papers bound to a single spine and sandwiched between covers - and the reason why it usurped the scroll, is that it allows for text on both sides of the paper and yet still provides a continuous reading experience.
(Receipts) Printing on thermal paper does not mean adding ink to it. Rather, the ink is already encapsulated within the paper. The act on printing requires only a spark to heat up the paper.

Magnitude calculation: not exact answers but answers that are easily understandable and say something fundamental about the world using only the information available on a bus. They must be accurate by "an order of magnitude".
(Banknotes) Are the most sophisticated pieces of paper that have ever been made. They are a literal, material manifestation of the trust we all have in the whole economic system.

Electronic paper is a type of flat screen that displays text using real ink and is designed to be read with reflective light bouncing off it in the same way as a physical book. The difference is that electronic paper can be controlled digitally to display any text required almost instantly.
Books on shelves and on tables are a kind of internal marketing exercise, reminding us who we are and who we want to be.
Concrete
Concrete doesn't dry out. Quite the opposite, water is an ingredient of concrete.
Gels are semisolid an wobbly types of matter. It doesn't slosh around like a liquid because it has an internal skeleton that prevents the liquid moving.
With concrete, if you can build the mold, you can create the structure.

There are two ways of breaking a material: one is break it plastically, and one is is to create a crack though it. Concrete breaks in the second way, the one that takes less energy. The Romans never solved this problem and so only used concrete in situations where it was being compressed rather than stretched. Joseph's solution was to embed loops of steel inside the concrete, he couldn't have known that the cement bonds very well to steel. Joseph couldn't have known that steel and concrete have almost identical coefficients of expansion.

Concrete was being continually cast. It arrived by truck at the bottom of the building and was pumped up into a mold at the top. Meanwhile, the mold, which was the size and shape of a floor of the building, was fitted with steel rods that would become the internal skeleton of the concrete tower. Once a floor had been cast, it was then used to support the mold, which was moved up a story, and so the process was repeated. The capacity of the machinery to pump concrete vertically to the top of that tower proved to be a severe problem.

Self-healing concrete has B. pasteurii bacteria embedded inside it along with a form of starch, which acts as food for the bacteria. Under normal circumstances these bacteria remain dormant, but if cracks forms the bacteria are released and start to look around for food. They find starch, grow and replicate. Doing so they excrete calcite, that bonds the concrete and starts to build up a mineral structure that spans the crack.
Concrete cloth comes in a roll and needs only water to be added for it to harden into any shape you like.
Foam

Jelly (gel) is a liquid trapped in a solid prison, but one in which the prison bars are like an invisibly thin mesh. The liquid in a jelly can be replaced by other liquids. Kristler managed to separate the liquid of a jelly from its internal skeleton. He engineered a jelly in which the internal skeleton was made of the mineral silicon dioxide, "silica aerogel": the lightest solid in the world (99.8% of air, with density only three times greater than air). It is the best insulator in the world, but is as fragile and brittle as glass.
Glass

Sand is a mixture of tiny bits of stone that have fallen off larger bits of rock as a result of the wind and the waves and other wear and tear that stones have to put up with. A lot of them are made of quartz (regular arrangement of SiO2 molecules).

When the liquid water is cooled, crystal re-form with ease and create ice again. When liquid SiO2 cools down, the molecules find it very difficult to form a crystal again, the result is a solid material that has the molecular structure of a chaotic liquid: a glass.
It looks easy to create glass but it's not. Quartz will most certainly be full of bits of sand that didn't melt. You also need a temperature of around 1200°C.

Before the Romans, windows were open to the wind, and although these might have wooden shutters or cloth curtains to keep out excessive wind and rain, the idea that a transparent material might be able to provide complete protection was revolutionary.

Mirrors were simply metal surfaces, polished to a high shine. Romans realized that the addition of a layer of transparent glass would protect this metal surface from scratches and corrosion while allowing them to reduce the metal surface to a fraction of millimeter, reducing the cost of mirrors.
Within all atoms there is a majority of empty space. So the real question is not "Why is the glass transparent?", but "Why aren't all materials transparent?"

The way quanta are arranged in glass is such that moving to a free row requires much more energy than is available in visible light. So visible light has no choice but to pass straight through the atoms. Glass is opaque to higher energy light (e.g. UV). Opaque materials like wood and stone have lots of cheap seats available even for visible light.

If the light strikes the glass at an angle, different parts of the light will enter it and emerge from it at different instants, forcing them to travel momentarily at slightly different speeds. This is what makes optical lenses possible.
Glass made beer light, transparent and uniform. (Before glass people couldn't really see how the beer looked like).
Bulletproof glass has several layers of plastic in its middle.
Glass is a material that allows us to transcend our scale. But we have no great love for the material. Is smooth, transparent, and cold. These are not human qualities.
It is inert and invisible, not just optically, but culturally.
Graphite:
The biggest diamond yet discovered is located in the Milky Way. It is an entire planet five times the size of Earth. The biggest yet found is the size of a football.
Because of its hardness, virtually nothing can scratch it.
Another remarkable attribute of diamond: it's extremely light.

"Diamonds are forever", DeBeers invented the idea of the diamond engagement ring as the only true way to express everlasting love. All diamonds, though, are actually turning slowly into graphite. But it takes billion of years.

In the graphite structure, the outer electrons do not just bond with a counterpart electron in a neighboring atom but rather form a sea of electrons within the material. That's why graphite conducts electricity and is opaque (intra-layer highest cohesion forces extra-layer low cohesion forces).
Synthetic diamonds don't work because: they are mostly colored and flawed, much of the value of diamonds derives from their authenticity and they are still very expensive.
Lonsdaleite is another way of arranging carbon that produces an harder substances than carbon.
Carbon fiber is made by spinning graphite into a fiber, rolling sheets of this material up, with fibers running lengthwise, using an epoxy glue to overcome the low extra-layer cohesion.
Other two shapes of carbon: one that looks like a giant football, and carbon nanotubes (they have the highest strength-to-weight ration of any material on the planet.

Graphene, a single layer of graphite. Is the thinnest, strongest, and stiffest material in the world, it conducts heat faster than any other material, it can carry more electricity, faster and with less resistance, than any other material. The most intriguing claim is that it is a two-dimensional material. It cannot be thinner or thicker and be the same material.
Porcelain
We don't have materials that can withstand the temperatures required to contain melted ceramics.
Clay is a mixture of finely powdered minerals and water. When is heated, first water evaporates, then bridges between minerals atoms are built.

If earthenware was covered with a particular kind of ash, this ash would transform during firing into a glass coating that would stick to the outside of the pot. This glass would seal all the pores on the outside and the pots could be colored and decorated (tiles).
If you add kaolin and you cook at very high temperature (1300°C), you get porcelain.
From China they exported not just the porcelain but the tea-drinking ritual as well.

The ringing sound of a cup is the clearest and surest way to know whether it is fully formed inside. Tap a terra cotta cup and you will hear almost nothing, or a dull thud at best. But because the porcelain is fully dense, you can hear the strength and vitality in its ring.
Implant
Plaster is a ceramic made of dehydrated mineral gypsum, which when mixed with water becomes hard like cement. When mixed with cotton bandages it becomes much tougher.

They used a part of my own hamstring to remodel my anterior cruciate ligament, but in order to attach it mechanically to my knee he had to use some screws. Our bodies are very picky about materials inserted into them. Most things are rejected, but titanium is one of the metals they will tolerate. It will undergo osseointegration, which means that it will form strong bonda with living bone.
What makes us old is not the age of our cells but the deterioration of the system that generate them.

Synthetic implants are a radical solution to the problem of some parts of the body waring out before the rest, but they are not a solution to the ultimate problem (if we can call it that) of death: what they offer is a better kind of life.
Synthesis

Although a material may look and feel monolithic, this is an illusion: materials are, in fact, composed of many different entities that combine to form the whole, and these different entities reveal themselves at different scales.
Iron, oxygen, silicon, magnesium, sulfur, nickel, calcium and aluminium make up 98.8 percent of the mass of the Earth. The rest are technically trace elements, including carbon.

Our bodies are mostly made of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen, and yet through subtle rearrangements of the molecular structure of these ingredients, and the sprinkling of a few minerals such as calcium and potassium, an immense diversity of biomaterials results, from hair, to bone, to skin. Knowing the basic chemical composition is not enough to understand materiality.
Silicon chips, strangely enough they contains no moving parts, using only electric and magnetic properties of materials to control the flow of information.
The multi scale architecture that inhabits all of the stuff around us explains why all metals may look the same but behave very differently.

Living matter is, in some sense, no different conceptually from non-living matter. What distinguish them is that living materials actively organizes their internal architecture by setting up communication between different scales. But the distinction is likely to become blurred.
For humans, materials are not just functional, there are also aesthetic and cultural reasons. They mean something, they embody our ideals, they give us part of our identity.

We are all sensitive to the meaning of materials, whether consciously or subconsciously. Designers and architects use these meanings to create clothes, products, and buildings that we like. In every aspect of our lives we choose materials that reflect our values.

There is a continual reflection, absorption, and expression going on in the material world. The desire for, say, stronger, more comfortable, waterproof, breathable fabrics creates a need for the understanding of the internal material architectures that are required to create them. Materials are a reflection of who we are, a multi-scale expression of our human needs and desires.
(Nothing underlined (so not in the list, but still interesting): Chocolate, Plastic)

paragraphs: Surely you're joking, Mr. Feynman notes
The book is very interesting, I'll just write down the sentences/quotes I liked:
I didn't like the symbols for sine, cosine, tangent, and so on. To me, "sin f" looked like s times i times n times f! So I invented another symbol.
I realized that if I'm going to talk to anybody else, I'll have to use the standard symbols, so I eventually gave up my own symbols.
I don't know what's the matter with people: they don't learn by understanding; they learn by some other way - by rote, or something. Their knowledge is so fragile!
People often think I'm a faker, but I'm usually honest, in a certain way - in such a way that often nobody believes me!
I sat with the physicists, but after a bit I thought: It would be nice to see what the rest of the world is doing, so I'll sit for a week or two in each of the other groups.
I started off by drawing an outline of the cat and began to name the various muscles.
"We know all that!"

"Oh" I say, "you do? Then no wonder I can catch up with you so fast after you've had four years of biology". They had wasted all their time memorizing stuff like that, when it could be looked up in fifteen minutes.

The mindreader explained that you hold onto their hands, loosely, and as you move, you jiggle a little bit. You come to an intersection, where you can go forward, to the left, or to the right. You jiggle a little bit to the left, and if it's incorrect, you feel a certain amount of resistance, because they don't expect you to move that way. But when you move in the right direction, because they think you might be able to do it, they give way more easily, and there is no resistance. So you must always be jiggling a little bit, testing out which seems to be the easiest way.
Von Neumann gave me an interesting idea: that you don't have to be responsible for the world you're in.

I was always dumb in that way. I never knew who I was talking to. I was always worried about the physics. If the idea looked lousy, I said it looked lousy. If it looked good, I said it looked good. Simple preposition.

It was a brilliant idea: You have no responsibility to live up to what other people think you ought to accomplish. I have no responsibility to be like they expect me to be. It's their mistake, not my failing.

That was dangerous: when you're away and you've got nothing but paper, and you're feeling lonely, you remember all the good things and you can't remember the reason you had the arguments. And it didn't work out. The arguments started again right away, and the marriage lasted for only two years.

When you're young, you have all these things to worry about - should you go there, what about your mother. And you worry, and try to decide, but then something else comes up. It's much easier to just plain decide. Never mind - nothing is going to change you mind. I did once when I was a student at MIT. I got sick and tired of having to decide what kind of dessert I was going to have at the restaurant, so I decided it would always be chocolate ice cream, and never worried about it again - I had the solution to that problem.

He thinks I'm following the steps mathematically, but that's not what I'm doing. I have the specific, physical example of what he's trying to analyze, and I know from instinct and experience the properties of the thing. So when the equations says it should behave so-and-so, and I know that's the wrong way around, I jump up and say, "Wait! There's a mistake!".

I thought how we teach physics: we have so many techniques that we never stop telling students how to do things. On the other hand, the drawing teacher is afraid to tell you anything. If your lines are very heavy, the teacher can't say, "Your lines are too heavy", because some artist has figured out a way of making great pictures using heavy lines.
I learned from her that every woman is worried about her looks, no matter how beautiful she is.

This famous problem: Nobody was permitted to see the Emperor of China and the question was, What is the length of the Emperor of China's nose? To find out, you go all over the country asking people what they think the length of the Emperor of China's nose is, and you average it.
(some complains about school system and school books)

The people from Japan believed they had only one way of moving up: to have their children educated more than they were; that it was very important for them to move out their peasantry to become educated.
I had once thought to take drugs, but I got kind of scared of that: I love to think, and I don't want to screw up the machine.
I believe there's nothing in hallucinations that has anything to do with anything external to the internal psychological state of the person who's getting the hallucinations.
What else is there that we believe? We have some knowledge of how to educate, how to treat criminals. Yet these things are said to be scientific, we study them.

If you're doing an experiment, you should report everything that you think might make it invalid - not only what you think is right about it. Try to give all of the information to help others to judge the value of your contribution; not just the information that leads to judgement in one particular direction or another. We've learned from experience that the truth will out.

The first principle is that you must not fool yourself - and you are the easiest person to fool. After you've not fooled yourself, it's easy not to fool other scientists. You just have to be honest in a conventional way after that.

I have just one wish for you - the good luck to be somewhere where you are free to maintain the kind of integrity I have described, and where you do not feel forced by a need to maintain your position in the organization, or financial support, or so on, to lose your integrity. May you have that freedom.
Nice mathematical tricks:
Pag. 222
Encounters:
Baba Ram Das (and taking psychedelic drugs): Pag. 376
Tao te ching notes
I underlined something almost on every page, I’ll try to take only important points:
Forewords/Introduction:
Tao Te Ching had been translated into English more often than any other book except the Bible.

Accept what is in front of you without wanting the situation to be other than it is. Study the natural order of things and work with it rather against it, for to try to change what is only sets up resistance. […] If we watch carefully, we will see that work proceeds more quickly and easily if we stop “trying”, if we stop making an extra effort, if we stop looking for results. […] (for more, pag. IX-X)
We are human beings, uniquely called to occupy a specific place the cosmic order, no matter where or in what era we live.
To be natural is not easy. Inwardly, it involves a state of openness or receptivity that is subtle, elusive, and active.

All phenomena everywhere depend upon the harmonious relationship of these forces called yin and yang, female and male, return and expression. To be fully human is to develop a power of attention that allows this relationship to take place within one’s own psychophysical space. The study that leads to the emergence of this consciousness within ourselves is known as the path, Tao. Meditation is the process of becoming familiar with one’s own real structure as a human being.

To be a warrior in the outer life, one must be a warrior in the inner life. To govern in the outer life, one must govern in the inner life. To be wise in the outer life, one must be wise in the inner life.
Book:
Under heaven all can see beauty only because there is ugliness.
All can know good as good only because there is evil.
If people lack knowledge and desire,
Then it is best not to interfere.
The wise are impartial;
They see people as they are.
The wise stay behind, and are thus ahead.
They are detached, thus at one with all.
Through selfless action, they attain fulfillment.
In dwelling, be close to the land.
In meditation, go deep in the heart.
In dealing with others, be gentle and kind.
In speech, be true.
In business, be competent.
In action, watch the timing.
Accept disgrace willingly.
Accept misfortune as the human condition.
[…] Accept being unimportant.
Do not be concerned with loss or gain.
[…] Misfortune comes from having a body.
[…] Surrender yourself humbly; then you can be trusted to care for all things.
Love the world as your own self; then you can truly care for all things.
Stay with the ancient Tao,
Move with the present.
Observers of the Tao do not seek fulfillment.
Not seeking fulfillment, they are now swayed by desire for change.
Empty yourself of everything.
Let the mind become still.
The ten thousand things rise and fall while the self watches their return.
They grow and flourish and then return to the source.
Not knowing constancy leads to disaster.
Those who do not trust enough will not be trusted.
[…] renounce wisdom, [...] renounce morality, […] renounce profit.
[…] It is more important
To see the simplicity,
To realize our true nature,
To cast off selfishness
And temper desire.
Everyone else is busy,
But I alone am aimless and without desire.
I am different.
I am nourished by the great mother.
From the very beginning until now its name has never been forgotten.
When you are at one with the Tao,
The Tao welcomes you.
When you are at one with the Virtue,
Virtue is always there.
When you are at one with the loss,
Loss is experienced willingly.
Those who stand on tiptoe are not steady.
[…] Those who put on a show are not enlightened.
[...] They do not bring happiness.
Therefore followers of the Tao avoid them.
The human being follows the earth.
Earth follows heaven.
Heaven follows the Tao.
Tao follows what is natural.
Know honor,
Yet remain humble.
The universe is sacred.
You cannot improve it.
If you try to change it, you will ruin it.
If you try to hold on to it, you will lose it.
Achieve results,
But never glory in them.
Achieve results,
Because is the natural way.
Achieve results,
But not through violence.
Knowing the others is wisdom;
Knowing the self is enlightenment
Mastering others require force;
Mastering the self needs strength.
The great Tao
[…] fulfils its purpose silently and makes no claim.
Soft and weak overcome hard and strong.
Tao abides in non-action,
Yet nothing is left undone.
Truly good people do nothing,
Yet leave nothing undone.
Foolish people are always doing,
Yet much remains to be done.
Therefore the humble is the root of the noble.
The low is the foundation of the high.
[…] Their utility is the source of their strength.
Being arises from not being.
For one gains by losing
And loses by gaining.
Teaching without words and working without doing
Are understood by very few.
Those who are attached to things will suffer greatly.
[…] Those who are contented are never disappointed.
There is no greater sin than craving,
No greater curse than discontent,
No greater misfortune than wanting something for ourselves.
When nothing is done, nothing is left undone.
The world is governed by letting things take their course.
It cannot be governed through interference.
Those who know how to live […] will not be wounded in battle. [...] Because they have no places for death to enter.
Respect of Tao and honour of Virtue are not demanded,
But they are in the nature of things.
Keep your mouth shut,
Guard the senses,
And life is always full.
Open your mouth,
Always be busy,
And life is beyond hope.
Be at one with the dust of the earth.
This is primal union.
Those who have achieved this state
Do not distinguish between friends and enemies,
Between good and harm, between honor and disgrace.
This is the highest state of being.
I take no action and people behave themselves.
I enjoy peace and people become honest.
I do nothing and people become rich.
I have no desires and people return to the good and simple life.
The wise are sharp but not cutting,
Pointed but not piercing,
Straightforward but not unrestrained,
Brilliant but not blinding.
Approach the universe with Tao,
And evil will have no power.
[…] We will not hurt one another.
Achieve greatness in small things.
[...] The wise do not attempt anything very big,
And thus achieve greatness.
A journey of a thousand miles starts under ones feet.
[…] Therefore the wise seek freedom from desire.
If you would guide the people, you must serve with humility.
If you would lead them, you must follow behind.
I have three treasure which I hold and keep.
The first is mercy; the second is economy;
The third is daring not to be ahead of others.
From mercy comes courage; from economy comes generosity;
From humility comes leadership.
Knowing ignorance is strength.
Ignoring knowledge is sickness.
When people lack a sense of awe, there will be disaster.
The Tao of heaven does not strive and yet it overcomes.
It does not speak and yet is answered.
Is does not ask, yet all its needs are met.
It seems to have no aim and yet its purpose is fulfilled.
If people are not afraid to die,
It is of no avail to threaten them with death.
The stiff and unbending is the disciple of death.
The gentle and yielding is the disciple of life.
Truthful words are not beautiful.
Beautiful words are not truthful.
Good people do not argue.
Those who argue are not good.
Those who know are not learned.
The learned do not know.
The wise never try to hold on to things.
The more you do for others, the more you have.
The more you give to others, the greater your abundance.
The Tao of heaven is sharp but does not harm
The Tao of the wise is to work without effort.
Notes, comments, and echoes:

Addiction or craving, which is what desire becomes when we allow it to absorb the finer energies of our psyche. Craving is a desire that devours us. But desires pure and simple are not to be killed or suppressed; they are an aspect of our human nature.
To remain whole, be twisted!
To become straight, let yourself be bent.
To become full, be hollow.
Be tattered, that you may be renewed.
Genuine goodness is action that springs spontaneously from the vital centre go oneself, not merely action done in conformity to an ideal, however noble, that is held by thought.
"All actions take place in time by the interweaving of the forces of Nature; but the man lost in selfish delusion thinks that himself is the actor."
When the heart weeps for what it has lost,
The Spirit laughs for what it has found.
Our lives are a reflection of the quality of our attention.
Keep your own cleverness from making the Way into merely mental information.
Socrates’ wisdom consists in the awareness that he is not wise.
Nirvana (freedom) is samsara (slavery). Nirvana is the total awareness of samsara; freedom Ia the total awareness of slavery; knowledge is the total awareness of ignorance.
The 4-hour work week notes
Notes (only the one that I really though important, for all of them take the book):

The New Rich (NR) are those who abandon the deferred-life plan and create luxury lifestyles in the present using the currency of the New Rich: time and mobility. This is an art and a science we will refer to as Lifestyle Design (LD).
People don't want to be millionaires, they want to experience what they believe only millions can buy.

Money is multiplied in practical value depending on the number of W's you control in your life: what you do, when you do it, where you do it, an with whom you do it. I call this "freedom multiplier". Options, the ability to choose, is the real power.

Ask for forgiveness, not permission. It it isn't going to devastate those around you, try it and then justify it. People deny things on an emotional basis that they can learn to accept after the fact.

"I'll just work unitl I have X dollars and then do what I want." If you don't define the "what I want" alternate activities, the X figure will increase indefinitely to avoid the fear-inducing uncertainty of this void.
Just a few words on time management: Forget all about it. Enter the world of elimination.
Keep in mind: doing something unimportant well does not make it important, requiring a lot of time does not make a task important.
80% of the outputs result from 20% of the inputs.
Slow down and remember this: Most things make no difference. Being busy is a form of laziness, lazy thinking and indiscriminate action. Lack of time is actually lack of priorities.
Parkinson's Law dictates that a task will swell in (perceived) importance and complexity in relation to the time allotted for its completion.
To increase productivity:
limit tasks to the important to shorten work time (80/20)
shorten work time to limit tasks to the important(Parkinson's Law)
How to be effective in your job:
Steer people toward the means of communication, in order of preference: e-mail, phone, in-person meeting.
Meetings should only be held to make decisions about a predefined situation, not to define the problem.
Define the end time of meetings.
"No" should be your default answer to all requests.
Why not combine a mini-retirement with dentistry (or medical) geoarbitrage ad finance your trip with the savings?

Becoming a member of the NR is not just about working smarter. It's about building a system to replace yourself. If I can do it better than an assistant, why should I pay them at all? Because the goal is to free your time to focus on bigger and better things. It is absolutely necessary that you realize that you can always do something more cheaply yourself. This doesn't mean you want to spend your time doing it.

Unless something is well-defined and important, no one should do it. Eliminate before you delegate. Never automate something that can be eliminated, and never delegate something that can be automated or streamlined.
Mistakes of beginner bosses (for virtual assistants):
Accept the first person the firm provided and make no special requests at the outset.

Give imprecise directions. Sentences should have one possible interpretation and be suitable for a 2nd-grade reading level. Ask foreign VA to rephrase tasks to confirm understanding before getting started.
Give him a license to waste time.
Set the deadline a week in advance.
Give him too many tasks and don't set an order of importance.
You don't want to run a business, you want to own a business and spend no time on it.
Be a member of your target market an don't speculate what others need or will be willing to buy.

"Expert" in the context of selling product means that you know more about the topic than the purchaser. Expert status can be created in less than four weeks if you understand basic credibility indicator. There is a difference between being perceived as expert and being one.
Intuition and experience are poor predictors of which products and businesses will be profitable.

The more option you offer to the customer, the more indecision you create and the fewer orders you receive. The more option you offer to the customer, the more manufacturing and customer service burden you create for yourself.
Ask for two days so that, in the case your boss refuses, you can ask for just one as a fallback position. You need to ask for an inch and turn into a foot without setting off panic alarms.
Going into a project or job without defining when worthwhile becomes wasteful is like going into a casino without a cap on what you will gamble: dangerous and foolish.
Tens of thousands of people, most of them less capable than you, leave their jobs every day.
Relocation to one place for one to six months before going home or moving to another locale. The mini-retirement is not an escape from your life but a reexamination of it.

Learn to slow down. Get lost intentionally. Observe how you judge both yourself and those around you. Chances are that it's been a while. Take at least two months to disincorporate old habits and rediscover yourself without the reminder of a looming return flight.
I know too well that it's easier to live with ourselves if we cite an external reason for inaction.
Don't assume that places abroad are more dangerous than your home town. Most aren't.
Take less with you. Rather than pack for all contingencies, bring the absolute minimum and allocate $100-300 for purchasing things after you arrive and as you travel.

I am 100% convinced that most big questions we feel compelled to face use terms so undefined as to make attempting to answer them a complete waste of time. Until the question is clear, there is no point answering it. Have I decided on a single meaning for each term in this question? Can an answer to this question be acted upon to improve things? If you can't define it or act upon it, forget it.
What can I do with my time to enjoy life and feel good about myself? Continual learning and service.
