A critical moment occurs during mind-wandering when you suddenly realize you're no longer observing the breath. Loosing your focus wan't something you did, it happens unconsciously. And how do you train something that happens unconsciously? Simply take a moment to enjoy and appreciate "waking up" from mind-wandering. Avoid becoming annoyed or self-critical about mind-wandering. You should positively reinforce introspective awareness.
Repeat yourself 'beginning, end, beginning, end', as beginning and end of respectively in-breath and out-breath.
We believe we are the masters of our own minds, but there is no self in control of the mind.

Impatience is an emotion. Act as you should act with all the emotions while meditating. Don't identify with it by thinking 'I am impatient'. Regard it as just one more feeling that arises and passes away, thinking 'Impatience is arising'.
Subtle distraction is when less time is spent on the distraction, and the meditation object remains the primary focus. Gross distraction is when the meditation object slips into the background.

Catch distraction before they cause you to forget. To do this, try to recognize three or four distinct sensations between beginning and end of the in-breath. That will make following breath more interesting and extend the period of attention. You can also observe two pauses closely, and notice which is longer and which is shorter. Are the breaths longer than they were earlier? Is that related to how agitated is your mind?
Identify the distraction in the very moment you realize you're no longer on the breath. Use simple, natural label. Then, gently direct the attention back to the breath.
You aren't trying to eliminate the distractions entirely from awareness. As long as they stay in the background, let them come, let them be, and let them go.
If the urge to move becomes irresistible, decide in advance when you'll move, what movement you'll make, and be very observant as you perform that movement.

If you feel you're falling asleep and you can't continue: either take three deep breaths, filling lungs as much as possible, holding for a moment and exhaling forcefully, or tense all muscles in your body till you begin tremble slightly.

Are you your thoughts? Are you your feelings? Keep asking these questions.
Don't try to strong-arm your mind into a state of calm. Relax. Let it happen on its own. Allow other sensations and mental events in your peripheral awareness just to be there.

Recognize when a subtle distraction has the potential to become a gross distraction before it happens. Introspective awareness is watching your mind while the mind watches the breath.
Interesting insights, that tempts you to take notice, seems profound during meditation, but afterward appear trivial. Make a mental not of them and address them after meditation.
If a powerful thought keeps returning, acknowledge it, allow it, accept it, and make it your temporary meditation object, without analyzing its content.
Dullness occurs when we reduce the flow of thought and sensations. Therefore, the overall energy level drops.
Three steps to defeat dullness: recognize its presence and rise from it, notice when it returns, and repeat until dullness doesn't come back.

Moments of Consciousness model: we can only be conscious of information coming from one sense organ at a time. Each mind moment provides only a single "object" of consciousness. They can be: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, mind sense (thoughts or emotions) and binding moment (integrates the information provided by other senses). The product of the first six senses is stored in a "working memory", and the seventh project into consciousness an integrated version of those.

Any moment of consciousness can be a moment of attention (and contain few objects) or a moment of peripheral awareness (and containing many objects). It can be non-perceiving when none of the sense organs provides them with any content. The energy level of the mind depends on the ration of perceiving to non-perceiving moments. We can also use intention to determine the objects of subsequent moments of consciousness.
Forgetting, gross and subtle distraction and exclusive focus depends on the proportion of moments of attention in a given period whose object is the sensation of breath, versus some distraction.
Mindfulness means that the balance between moments of attention and of awareness is just right. Dullness is determined by by the proportion of non-perceiving moments.

Dullness of any kind is always pleasant, except when we actively resist. If some disturbance causes you to jerk or feel startled, or if you're surprised finding yourself taking a deep breath, or when you find yourself correcting for a slumping posture, dullness was probably present.

Body scanning is systematically investigate discrete body areas, examining all sensations, but looking in particular for sensations that changes with the breath. Use that when subtle distractions aren't too strong, and when attention and peripheral awareness are fairly clear.

The Mind-System: the mind is made up of many distinct but interconnected processes. This complex system is composed of two main parts, the conscious mind, the part of psyche we experience directly, and the conscious mind, related to the "behind the scenes" activities.
Part of conscious mind: visual, auditory, olfactory, gustatory, somatosensory, mental and binding moments of consciousness.

Part of unconscious mind: sensory mind (made of five sub-minds), that process the info from the five physical senses, and discriminating mind (made of several sub-minds), that produces moments of consciousness with mental objects, such thought and emotions.

When thoughts, emotions, sense-percepts and hedonic feelings are projected into consciousness, this info becomes available as input for the other minds. Each sub-mind performs its own specialized task independently of others, and all at the same time. The conscious mind is the universal recipient and source of information. Intentions are generated by unconscious sub-mind, and this can become a distraction if we're meditating. Conscious intentions, repeatedly acted upon, eventually give raise to automatic actions that no longer require conscious intention.

Conscious intention is the key to develop exclusive attention. Hold the intention to observe the meditation object, and hold the intention to ignore everything else. To train that, try experiencing the whole body with the breath: gradually expand the scope of your attention until it includes sensations related to the breath throughout the entire body. After a while shift your focus back to the breath st the nose. When exclusive focus start to fade, repeat the entire exercise.
As we start pacifying the mind, we can experience the breath purely as a sensory phenomenon, free from conceptualizations. Your meditation object has finally become the sensations of the breath.

Flow is a state of concentration so focused that it amounts to a complete absorption in activity. With the right conditions, you can enter in flow state while meditating. People feel strong, alert, in effortless control, unselfconscious, and at the peak of their abilities. Both the sense of time and emotional problems seem to disappear, and there is an exhilarating feeling of transcendence.
Seven conditions for an activity to lead to a state of flow:
Performed as an end in itself, not for any other purpose.
The goal are clear, and the feedback immediate.
It's neither too difficult, nor too easy, it's perfectly balanced.
Requires complete focus of attention.
There is no sense of a self apart from the activity.
A feeling of effortlessness arises.
There is a sense of successfully exercising control.
Everything from Stage Seven onward happens not because our skills improve any further, but because the mind-system itself start functioning differently.
Five grades of piti:
Brief, unpredictable episodes, with only one or few unusual sensations or involuntary body movements happening at once.
Brief episodes with a grater number of different phenomena occurring at the same time.
Episodes last longer and their intensity alternately increases and decreases.
Intense and sustained manifestation of physical pliancy.
Full maturation of physical pliancy and meditative joy.
Don't feel like you're missing out if you don't encounter the peculiar experiences that make up the various grades of pity. Some people don't.
Please don't make the mistake of blaming yourself if you have difficulties in meditation.
We need to be mindful of our thoughts, emotions, and behavior at all times, you can no longer separate meditation from the rest of your life.

The path to complete pacification can be summoned up in a single word: diligence. Diligence means constantly persevering. In dry period you just have to have confidence in your abilities and trust that it's a process that just takes time to mature. Cultivate an attitude of acceptance and patience.
"Things" don't actually exists. "Process" is all there is.
Is no that the world doesn't exists. The world you perceive, your personal reality, is nothing more than a construct of your mind.

Walking meditation
You fix the attention on the soles of your feet, rather than on the breath at the nose.
Don't think of walking meditation as a break from your practice. If you need a break, so something completely different.
The best location is outdoors, open space where you won't be interrupted. Use a path you can follow easily.
Thirty minutes is a good period.
When you catch your mind wandering, simply bring yourself back to the present by focusing your attention on the sensations in your feet.
The walking meditation just described should feel pleasant, relaxing, and easy.
Analytical meditation
Analytical meditation means thinking about something. Carefully choose a topic and systematically examine it with a stable, clear, and focus mind.
Topics of analytical meditation fall into three categories:
Teaching, doctrines , or other ideas you wish to understand more deeply.
Problems you want to solve or decisions you need to make.
Experiences, thoughts, or realizations that seem to point to a valuable insight.
Do not interrupt your samatha-vipassana practice, plan an additional session of analytical meditation.
Stages:
Preparation: focus on ideas and information relevant to a solution.

Incubation: combine and recombine all the relevant information, searching among those new combinations for a solution. Compare present problem and its potential solutions with similar past problems and their actual solutions.
Solution: It can happen in the conscious phase or in the unconscious, but in most cases both of them have contributed to that solution.
Verification: It happen in the consciousness, verifying the solution got through logical analysis.
(Now it start explaining how to do that in meditation, read it on the book if you want. It involves "talking" to the problem...)

This meditation conditions your mind to readily enter a state of ease, peace, love, and happiness.
Generate the feelings through making wishes (may I be free from suffering, may I be free from ill will, ...), calling to mind how it is to be in that way.

Generate the wish for other, picturing the person as clear as you can. First of all do that thinking of someone you care about, then someone you are not so close to, then someone you encounter sometimes but you don't really know, and finally someone you have difficulties with.
Redirect those feelings to you.
(To get all from this kind of meditation, reread the wishes you can make)
Mindful review
You will regularly review and reflect on your thoughts, emotions, speech and actions.
Steps for mindful review:
Set aside a period of up to half an hour each day.
Choose several events that stand out as particularly unwholesome activities of body, speech, or mind.
Two-part review:

Recall how much mindfulness you had during the event and consider what might have been different had you been more mindful. Evoke the details, reflect on the degree of mindfulness as the event unfolded, think about where the attention was focused, then consider the consequences of your behavior. If you regret something, resolve to bring more mindfulness to similar situations and consider whether there's anything you can do to reverse or compensate for the adverse effects of anything you regret having done. There is no place for guilt, blame or self-recrimination, though.

Practice mindfulness with clear comprehension, focusing on the deeper intentions driving those particular thoughts , emotions, speech or actions. See if you can detect the craving behind your actions. The more often you decline to act out of craving, the less power craving has over you. There is far more happiness to be gained through increasing the happiness of others than through pursuing you own desires.

A event is unwholesome if it causes harm and suffering to yourself or others that is unnecessary and could be avoided. Acts in itself are always neutral, it's the consequences that make the difference.
Definitions:
Samatha: tranquility or calm abiding.
Vipassana: insight.
Samadhi: stable attention.
Sati: mindfulness.
Properties:
Samatha = Samadhi + Sati
Awakening = Samatha + Vipassana
Blissful dullness = Samatha + NOT Vipassana
Mind wandering = NOT Samatha + Vipassana
Samatha = Effortless attention + Mindfulness + Joy + Tranquility + Equanimity
Vipassana = impermanence+ emptiness + nature of suffering + causal interdependence of all phenomena + illusion of separate self
Nice motivational sentences
The only bad meditation session is the one you didn't do!
Thoughts become words, words become deeds, deeds becomes habit, habit becomes character, and character becomes destiny.
Goals of stages:
Learn how to prepare for practice and establish a consistent daily practice.
Shorten the period of mind-wandering and extend the period of sustained attention.
Overcome forgetting and falling asleep.
Overcome gross distraction and strong dullness.
Overcome subtle distraction and increase the power of mindfulness.
Subdue subtle distractions and develop metacognitive introspective awareness.
Effortlessly sustain exclusive attention and powerful mindfulness.
Complete pacification of the senses and full arising of meditative joy.
Maturation of meditative joy that produces tranquility and equanimity.
For the qualities of samatha to persist after yo rise from the cushion.
There is a formula!
S = P * R. The amount of suffering you experience is equal to actual pain multiplied by the mind's resistance to this pain.

file: The old man and the sea notes.html
paragraphs: The old man and the sea notes
Sentences I liked particularly:
“But I tried not to borrow. First you borrow. Then you beg.”
“Why do old men wake up so early? Is it to have one longer day?”
He did not remember when he had first started to talk aloud when he was by himself.
It was considered a virtue not to talk unnecessarily.
He did not say that because he knew that if you said a good thing it might not happen.
No one should be alien in their old age, he thought. But it is unavoidable.
I wonder if he has any plans or if he is just as desperate as I am.
I wish he would turn with the current. That would show that he was tiring.
But he stays down forever. Then I will stay down with him forever.
Now they were in hurricane months and, when there are no hurricanes, the weather of hurricane months is the best of all the year.
“Blessed Virgin, pray for the death of this fish. Wonderful though he is.”
There are three things that are brothers: the fish and my two hands.
“I told the boy I was a strange old man,” he said. “Now is then I must prove it.”

Then he was sorry for the great fish that had nothing to eat and his determination to kill him never relaxed in his sorrow for him. How many people will he feed, he thought. But are they worthy to eat him? No, of course not. There is no one worthy of eating him from the manner of his behaviour and his great dignity.
“It is not bad,” he said. “And pain does not matter to a man.”
I am only better than him through trickery and he meant me no harm.
It is silly not to hope, he thought. Besides I believe it is a sin.
You loved him when he was alive and you loved him after. It you loved him, it is not a sin to kill him.
You should have brought many things, he thought. But you did not bring them, old man. Now is no time to think of what you do not have. Think of what you can do with what there is.
The power of myth notes
Sentences:
"The fates lead him who will; him who won't they drag".

People say that what we're all seeking is a meaning for life. I don't think that's what we're really seeking. I think that what we're seeking is an experience of being alive, so that our life experiences on the purely physical plane will have resonances within our own innermost being and reality, so that we actually feel the rapture of being alive.

There's no meaning. What's the meaning of the universe? What's the meaning of a flea? It's just there. That's it. And your own meaning is that you're there. We're so engaged in doing things to achieve purposes of outer value that we forget that the inner value, the rapture that is associated with being alive, is what it's all about.
Society has provided young people no rituals by which they become members of the tribe, of the community.

Now, what is a myth? The dictionary definition of a myth would be stories about gods. So then you have to ask the next question: What is a god? A god is a personification of a motivating power of a value system that functions in human life and in the universe - the powers of your own body and of nature.
Myths basically serves four functions:
Mystical function: realizing what a wonder the universe is, and what a wonder you are, and experiencing awe before this mystery.
Cosmological dimension: showing you what the shape of the universe is, but showing it in such a way that the mystery again comes through.
Sociological function: supporting and validating a certain social order.
Pedagogical function: how to live a human lifetime under any circumstances.

The earth does not belong to man, man belongs to the earth. All things are connected like the blood that unites us all. Man did not weave the web of life, he is merely a strand in it. Whatever he does to the web, he does to himself.
At the bottom of the abyss comes the voice of salvation. The black moment is the moment when the real message of transformation is going to come. At the darkest moment comes the light.
Heaven and hell are within us, and all the gods are within us.
The myth is the public dream and the dream is the private myth.

Everything we know is within the terminology of the concepts of being and not being, many and single, true and untrue. We always think in terms of opposites. But God, the ultimate, is beyond the pairs of opposites, that is all there is to it.

Aristophanes says that in the beginning there were creatures composed of what are now two human beings. And those were of three sorts: male/female, male/male, and female/female. The gods the split them all in two. But after they had been split apart, all they could think of to do was to embrace each other again in order to reconstitute the original units. So we all now spend our lives trying to find and re-embrace out other halves.

Eternity isn't some later time. Eternity isn't even a long time. Eternity has nothing to do with time. Eternity is that dimension of here and now that all thinking in temporal terms cuts off. And if you don't get it here, you won't get it anywhere. The problem with heaven is that you will be having such a good time there, you won't even think of eternity. You'll just have this unending delight in the beatific vision of God. But the experience of eternity right here and now, in all things, whether thought of as good or as evil, is the function of life.

Killing is not simply slaughter, it's a ritual act, as eating is when you say grace before meals. A ritual act is a recognition of your dependency on the voluntary giving of this food to you by the animal who has given its life. The hunt is a ritual.
These people didn't think of animals the way we do, as some subspecies. Animals are our equals at least, and sometimes our superiors.

Scholars speculate that they had to do with the initiation of boys into the hunt. Boys had to learn not only to hunt but how to respect animals, and what rituals to perform, and how in their own lives no longer to be little boys but to be men.

A woman has her first menstruation. It happens to her. Nature does it to her. She is identical with the earth goddess in her powers, and she has got to realize that about herself. The boy does not have an happening of this kind, so he has to be turned into a man and voluntarily become a servant of something greater than himself.

Suicide is also a symbolic act. It casts off the psychological posture that you happen to be in at the time, so that you may come into a better one. You die to your current life in order to come to another of some kind. But, as Jung says, you'd better not get caught in a symbolic situation. You don't have to die, really, physically. All you have to do is die spiritually and be reborn to a larger way of living.

You may have a success in life, but then just think of it - what kind of life was it? What good was it - you've never done the thing you wanted to do in all your life. Go where your body and soul want to go. When you have the feeling, then stay with it, and don't let anyone throw you off.
Consciousness is transformed either by the trials themselves or by illuminating revelations. Trials and revelations are what it's all about.
Our life evokes our character. You find out more about yourself as you go on. That's why it's good to be able to put yourself in situations that will evoke your higher nature rather than your lower.

When you are doing something that is a brand-new adventure, breaking new ground, whether it is something like a technological breakthrough or simply a way of living that is not what the community can help you with, there's always the danger of too much enthusiasm, of neglecting certain mechanical details. Then you fall off. "A dangerous path is this". When you follow the path of your desire and enthusiasm and emotion, keep your mind in control, and don't let it pull you compulsively into disaster.

A legendary hero is usually the founder of something - the founder of a new age, the founder of a new religion, the founder of a new city, the founder of a new way of live. In order to found something new, one has to leave the old and go in quest of the seed idea, a germinal idea that will have the potentiality of bringing forth that new thing.

Anyone brought up in an extremely strict, authoritative social situation is unlikely ever to come to the knowledge of himself. A good teacher is there to watch the young person and recognize what the possibilities are - then to give advice, not commands.

If the person insists on a certain program, and doesn't listen to the demands of his own heart, he's going to risk a schizophrenic crackup. Such a person has put himself off center. He has aligned himself with a program for life, and it's not the one the body's interested at all. The world is full of people who have stopped listening to themselves or have listened only to their neighbors to learn what they ought to do, how they ought to behave, and what the values are that they should living for.
"One way or another, we all have to find what best fosters the flowering of our humanity in this contemporary life, and dedicate ourselves to that."
"Not the first cause, but a higher cause?"

"I would say, a more inward cause. 'Higher' is just up there, and there is no 'up there'. We know that. That old man up there has been blown away. You've got to find the Force inside you. This is why Oriental gurus are so convincing to young people today. They say, 'It is in you. Go and find it'"

Each of us is a completely unique creature and if we are ever to give any gift to the world, it will have to come out of our own experience and fulfillment of our own potentialities, not someone else's.

You have to become an adult at a particular age. The age might be a good average age for that to happen - but actually, in the individual life, it differs greatly. Some people are late bloomers and come to a particular stages at a relatively late age. You have to have a feeling for where you are. You've got only one life to live, and you don't have to live it for six people. Pay attention to it.

Keep your mind on those moments when you feel most happy, when you really are happy - not excited, not just thrilled, but deeply happy. This requires a little bit of self-analysis. What is that makes you happy? Stay with it, no matter what people tell you. This is what I call "following your bliss".
"The adventure is its own reward - but it's necessarily dangerous, having both negative and positive possibilities, all of them beyond control."
"It's easier to stay home, stay in the womb, not take the journey."
"Yes, but then life can dry up because you're not off on your own adventure."
Love thine enemies because they are the instruments of your destiny.

She was in spiritual as well as physical pain. I told her that if she wanted release, she should affirm and not deny her suffering was her life, and that through it she had become the noble creature that she now was.

The more challenging or threatening the situation or context to be assimilated and affirmed, the greater the stature of the person who can achieve it. The demon that you can swallow gives you its power, and greater life's pain, the greater life's reply.
"The only one to blame is oneself. That's the helpful thing about the Indian idea of karma. Your life is the fruit of your own doing. You have no one to blame but yourself."
"But what about a chance? A drunken drier turns the corner and hits you. That isn't your fault. You haven't done that to yourself."
"Is there anything in your life that did not occurs by chance? This is a matter of being able to accept chance."

The place to find is within yourself. Nirvana is right here, in the midst of the turmoil of life. It is the state you find when you are no longer driven to live by compelling desires, fears, and social commitments, when you have found your center of freedom and can act by choice out of that.

The mother's right there. You're born from your mother, and she's the one who nurses you and instructs you and brings you up to the age when you must find your father. Now, the finding of the father has to do with finding of your own character and destiny.

And do you know who that god is? It's you. All of these symbols is mythology refer to you. You can get stuck out there, and think it's all out there. So you're thinking about Jesus with all the sentiments relevant to how he suffered - out there. But that suffering is what ought to be going on in you. Have you been spiritually reborn? Have you died to your animal nature and come to life as a human incarnation of compassion?

I come into this society, so I've got to live in terms of this society. It's ridiculous not to live in terms of this society because, unless I do, I'm not living. But I mustn't allow this society to dictate to me how I should live. One has to build up one's own system that may violate the expectations of the society, and sometimes society doesn't accept that.
Love itself is a pain, you might say - the pain of being truly alive.
You say, "Well, there must be somebody generating that energy"? Why do you have to say that? Why can't the ultimate mystery be impersonal?

When the center of the hearth is touched, and a sense of compassion awakened with another person or creature, and you realize that you and that other are in some sense creatures of the one life in being, a whole new stage of life in the spirit opens out.
"None but a god can worship a god".

The world "religion" means religio, linking back. If we say it is the one life in both of us, then my separate life has been linked to the one life, religio, linked back. This has become symbolized in the images of religion, which represent that connecting link.
Good ideas:
You don't teach until you are asked. You don't force your mission down people's throats (oriental).
Deep thoughts:
Pag. 42-43, about buying lands (from Chief Seattle, one of the last spokesmen of that Paleolithic moral order).
Suggested books:
Finnegans Wake
Ulysses
The power of now notes
Insights:
In essence there is and always has been only one spiritual teaching, although it comes in many forms.
Buddha's simple definition of enlightenment is "the end of suffering".
"Being" is the eternal, ever-present One Life beyond the myriad forma of life that are subject to birth and death.

The word God has become empty of meaning through thousands of years of misuse. The people who have never even glimpsed the realm of the sacred, the infinite vastness behind that word, use it with great conviction, as if they knew what they are talking about.

What is the greatest obstacle to experiencing this reality? Identification with your mind. The illusion of separateness, the illusion that there is you and a totally separate "other". You then forget that you are one with all that is. You can no longer feel this oneness as self-evident reality. You may believe it to be true, but you no longer know it to be true.

"I can't stop thinking altogether"."Then the mind is using you. You are unconsciously identified with it, so you don't even know that you are its slave.[...] The beginning of freedom is the realization that you are not the possessing entity - the thinker. Knowing this enables you to observe the entity. The moment you start watching the thinker, a higher level of consciousness becomes activated".
Start listening to the voice in your head as often as you can. This is what I mean by "watching the thinker". Listen to it impartially. That is to say, do not judge.

Instead of "watching the thinker", you can also create a gap in the mind stream simply by directing the focus of your attention into the Now. In this way, you draw consciousness away from mind activity and create a gap of no-mind in which you are highly alert and aware but not thinking. This is the essence of meditation. Pay attention to every step, every moment, even your breathing. Be totally present.

Emotions arises at the place where mind and body meet. It is the body's reaction to your mind - or you might say, a reflections of your mind in the body. The difference from thought to emotion is that, while a thought is in your head, an emotion has a strong physical component and so is primarily felt in the body. You can then allow the emotion to be there without being controlled by it. You no longer are the emotion: you are the watcher, the observing presence.

"What about positive emotions?". "Love, joy, and peace are deep states of Being or rather three aspects of the state of inner connectedness with Being. As such, they have no opposite. [...] In the unenlightened, mind-identified condition, what is sometimes wrongly called joy is the usually short-lived pleasure side of the continuously alternating pain/pleasure cycle. Pleasure is always derived from something outside you. whereas joy arises from within."
Don't seek to become free of desire or "achieve" enlightenment. Become present. Be there as the observer of the mind. Instead of quoting the Buddha, be the Buddha.

The greater part of human pain is unnecessary. It is self-created as long as the observed mind runs your life. The pain that you create now is always some form of nonacceptance, some form of unconscious resistance to what is.
Imagine asking an animal or a plant what time is it. Of course, they would answer that the time is now. What else is there?

If you no longer want to create pain for yourself and others, realize deeply that the present moment is all you ever have. Make the Now the primary focus of your life. Wheres before you dwelt in time and paid brief visits to the Now, Have your dwelling place in the Now and pay brief visits to past and future when required to deal with the practical aspects of your life situation.

Every emotional pain that you experience leaves behind a residue of pain that lives on in you. It's the emotional pain-body. It has two modes of being: dormant and active. Catch it the moment it awakens from its dormant state. The moment you observe it, feel its energy field within you, and take your attention into it, the identification is broken. A higher dimension of consciousness has come in. I call it presence. You are now the witness or the watcher of the pain-body.

Let me summarize the process. Focus attention on the feeling inside you. Know that is the pain-body. Accept that it is there. Don't think about it - don't let the feeling turn into thinking. Don't judge or analyze. Don't make an identity for yourself out of it. Stay present, and continue to be the observer of what is happening inside you. Become aware not only of the emotional pain but also of "the one who observes", the silent watcher. This is the power of the Now, the power of your own conscious presence. Then see what happens.

(in an argument) Once you have disidentified from your mind, whether you are right or wrong makes no difference to your sense of self at all, so the forcefully compulsive ad deeply unconscious need to be right, which is a form of violence, will no longer be there. Watch out for any kind of defensiveness within yourself. What are you defending? An illusory identity, an image in your mind, a fictitious entity.

Since the ego is a derived sense of self, it needs to identify with external things. It needs to be both defended and fed constantly. The most common ego identifications have to do with possessions, the work you do, social status and recognition, knowledge and education, physical appearance, special abilities, relationships, personal and family history, belief systems, and often political, nationalistic, racial, religious, and other collective identifications. None of these is you.

To be identified with your mind creates an endless preoccupation with past and future, because the past gives you an identity and the future holds the promise of salvation, of fulfillment in whatever form. Both are illusions.

Have you ever experienced, done, thought , or felt anything outside the Now? Nothing ever happened in the past; it happened in the Now. Nothing will ever happen in the future; it will happen in the Now.
In life-threatening emergency situations, the shift in consciousness from time to presence sometimes happens naturally.
In the Now, in the absence of time, all your problems dissolve. Suffering needs time; it cannot survive in the Now.
The mind cannot know the tree. It can only know facts or information about the tree. My mind cannot know you, only labels, judgments, facts, and opinions about you.
The future is usually imagined as either better or worse than the present. Both are illusory.

Use time in practical aspects of your life, but immediately return to present-moment awareness. Any lesson from the past becomes relevant and is applied now. Any planning as well as working toward achieving a particular goal is done now. If you made a mistake in the pas and dwell on it mentally, and self-criticism, remorse, or guilt come up, then you are making a mistake. If you become excessively focused on the goal, the Now is no longer honored. You're life journey is no longer an adventure, just an obsessive need to arrive, to attain, to "make it".

Unease, anxiety, tension, stress, worry - all forms of fear - are caused by too much future, and not enough presence. Guilt, regret, resentment, grievance, sadness, bitterness, and all forms of nonforgiveness are caused by too much past, and not enough presence.

If all your problems or perceived causes of suffering or unhappiness were miraculously removed for you today, but you had not become more present, more conscious, you would soon find yourself with a similar set of problems or causes of suffering.

You cannot be both unhappy and fully preset in the Now. Look around. Be aware of the silent presence of each thing. B aware of the space that allows everything to be. Listen to the sounds; don't judge them. Listen to the silence underneath the sounds.

"But my problems haven't been solved." "There are no problems, only situations - to be dealt with now, or to be left alone and accepted as part of the "isness" of the present moment until they change or can be dealt with."
"Would we still be able or willing to pursue external goals?" "Of course, but you will not have illusory expectations that anything or anybody in the future will save you or make you happy."
Everything is honored, but nothing matters.
"Am I at ease at this moment?" is a good question to ask yourself frequently. Or "What's going on inside me at this moment?".

See if you can catch yourself complaining. To complain is always nonacceptance of what is. If you find your here and now intolerable and it makes you unhappy, you have three options: remove yourself from the situation, change it, or accept it totally.
You can run without projecting yourself into the future and without resisting the present. As you move, work, run - do it totally.

"Large-scale waiting" is waiting for the next vacation, for a better job, for the children to grow up, for a truly meaningful relationship, for success, to make money, to be important, to become enlightened. Is not uncommon for people to spend their whole life waiting to start living. Waiting is a state of mind.
The only thing that is ultimately real about your life journey is the step you are taking at this moment.
Close your eyes and say to yourself "I wonder what my next thought is going to be". Then become very alert and wait for the next thought.

Everything that exists has Being, has God-essence, has some degree of consciousness. The human form turns into dust pretty quickly, is that tragic or cruel? Only if you create separate identity for each form.
"The teacher and the taught together create the teaching".
You can substitute "Christ" for presence. Never personalize Christ. Don't make Christ into form identity. Any kind of exclusivity is identification with form, and identification with form means ego.
Eternity doesn't mean endless time, but no time.
Please stop trying to understand Being. The mind will always try to squeeze it into a little box and then put a label on it. It cannot be done. It cannot become an object of knowledge.
Open you eyes and see the fear, the despair, the greed, and the violence that are all-pervasive. You don't need to condemn. Just observe. That is sin. That is insanity. That is unconsciousness.

What you perceive as a dense physical structure called body, is not ultimately real - is not you. You are your body. The body that you can see and touch is only a thin illusory veil. Underneath it lies the invisible inner body, the doorway into Being, into Life Unmanifested. The key is to be in a state of permanent connectedness with your inner body - to feel it all times.

Whenever you are waiting, wherever it may be, use that time to feel the inner body. In this way, traffic jams and line-ups become very enjoyable. Instead of mentally projecting yourself away from the Now, go more deeply into the Now by going more deeply into the body.

Whenever an answer, a solution, a creative idea is needed, stop thinking for a moment by focusing attention on your inner energy field. Become aware of the stillness. When you resume thinking, it will be fresh and creative.

When you listen you are giving the other person space - space to be. It is the most precious gift you can give. Most people don't know how to listen because the major part of their attention is taken up by thinking. They pay more attention to that than to what the other people is saying.

As you go about life, don't give 100 percent of your attention to the external world and to your mind. Keep some within. You feel it as a deep sense of peace somewhere in the background, a stillness that never leaves you, no matter what happens out there.
Your task is not to search for love, but to find a portal through which love can enter.

If there were nothing but silence, it wouldn't exist for you; you wouldn't know what it is. Only when sound appears does silence come into being. Similarly, if there were only space without any objects in space, it wouldn't exist for you.
There are two essential attributes of God, infinity and eternity.
"I always thought that true enlightenment is not possible except trough love in a relationship between a man and a woman".
"Has this happened to you?"
"I know that it will happen".
"You are waiting for an event in time to save you. Is this not the error that we have been talking about? Salvation is not elsewhere in place or time. It is here and now.
'When I obtain this or am free of that - I will be ok'. This is the unconscious mind-set that creates the illusion of salvation in the future. The joy of Being depends on nothing outside itself."

You see the time as the means to salvation, whereas in truth it is the greatest obstacle to salvation. You think that you can't get there from where and who you are at this moment because you are not yet complete or good enough, but the truth is that here and now is the only point from where you can get there. You "get" there by realizing that you are there already. You find God the moment you realize that you don't need to seek God.

It is not uncommon for couples to become addicted to those (love/hate) cycles. Their drama makes them feel alive. When a balance between the positive/negative polarities is lost and the negative, destructive cycles occur with increasing frequency and intensity, which tends to happen sooner or later, then it will be long before relationship finally collapses. Both polarities are different aspects of the same dysfunction. You become addicted to the other person.

Romantic love seems to offer liberation from state of fear, need, lack, and incompleteness that is part of the human condition in its unredeemed and unenlightened state. True love has no opposite. If it has an opposite, it is ego-need for a more complete and deeper sense of self, a need that the other person temporary meets. But there comes a point when your partner behaves in ways that fail to meet your needs, or rather those of your ego. You now perceive your partner as the cause of those feelings.

Every addiction arises from an unconscious refusal to face and move through your own pain. Every addiction starts with pain and ends with pain. Whatever the substance you are addicted to - alcohol, food, legal or illegal drugs, or a person - you are using something or somebody to cover up you pain.

Accepting what is, first you stop judging yourself;the you stop judging your partner. The greatest catalyst for change in a relationship is complete acceptance of your partner as he or she is, without needing to judge or change them in any way.
Love is state of Being. Your love is not outside; it is deep within you. You can never lose it, and it cannot leave you. It is not dependent on some other body, some external form.

Whenever a relationship is not working, is an opportunity for salvation. If there is anger, know that there is anger. If you observe unconscious behavior in your partner, hold it in the loving embrace of your knowing so that you won't react.
The moment you start to argue, you have identified with a mental position and are now defending not only that position but your sense of self. The ego is in charge. You have become unconscious.
Learn to give expression to what you feel without blaming. Learn to listen to your partner in an open, nondefensive way. Give you partner space for expressing himself or herself.

If you are consistently or at least predominantly present in your relationship, this will be the greatest challenge for you partner. They will not be able to tolerate your presence for very long and stay unconscious. If they are ready, they will walk through the door that you opened for them and join your state. If they are not, you will separate like oil and water. The light is too painful for someone who wants to remain in darkness.
As a general rule, the major obstacle for men tends to b the thinking mind, and the major obstacle for women the pain-body.

It is perfectly possible for an enlightened person, if the need for the male or female polarity is not met, to feel a sense of lack or incompleteness on the outer level of his or her being, yet at the same time be totally complete, fulfilled, and at peace within.

If you cannot be at ease with yourself when you are alone, you will seek a relationship to cover up your unease. You can b sure that the unease will then reappear in some other form within the relationship, and you will probably hold your partner responsible for it.
Conditions are neither positive nor negative. They are as they are. And when you live in complete acceptance of what is there is no "good" or "bad" in your life anymore.

If you forgive every moment - allow it to be as it is - then there will be no accumulation of resentment that needs to be forgiven at some later time. We are not talking of about happiness here. For example, when a loved one has just died, you cannot be happy. It is impossible. But you can be at peace. there might be sadness and tears, but provided that you have relinquished resistance, underneath the sadness you will feel a deep serenity, a stillness, a sacred presence.

The Buddha made this a central pat of his teaching. All conditions are highly unstable and in constant flux, or, as he put it, impermanence is a characteristic of every condition, every situation you will encounter in your life. It will change, disappear, or no longer satisfy you.
Things and conditions can give you pleasure, but they cannot give you joy. Nothing can give you joy. Joy is uncaused and arises from within as the joy of Being.
"All I have learned in the twenty years that I have been a monk I can sum up in one sentence: All that arises passes away. This I know."

Use negativity as a signal that reminds you to be more present. Just accept that it is there and take attention into the feeling. You are then in power - not in someone else's, nor are you run by your mind.

Surrender is the simple but profound wisdom of yielding to rather than opposing the flow of life. Surrender is to accept the present moment unconditionally and without reservation. It is perfectly compatible with taking action, initiation change or achieving goals.

In the state of surrender, you focus on one thing at a time. This doesn't mean you should not do any planning. It may well be that planning is the one thing you can do now. But make sure you don't start to run "mental movies".

So whenever any kind of disaster strikes, or something goes seriously "wrong", know that there is another side to it, that you are just one step away from something incredible: a complete alchemical transmutation of the base metal of pain and suffering into gold. You will not become happy, but fear and pain will become transmuted into an inner peace and serenity.

Don't turn away from the pain. Face it. Feel it fully. Feel it - don't think about it! Express it if necessary, but don't create a script in your mind around it. Give all your attention to the feeling, not to the person, event, or situation that seems have caused it. Don't let the mind use the pain to create victim identity for yourself out of it.
"Presence is the key. The Now is the key." "How will I know I have surrendered?" "When you no longer need to ask the question."

paragraphs: The subtle art of not giving a fuck notes
Counterintuitive insights:
Self-improvement and success often occur together. But that doesn't necessarily mean they're the same thing.
The key to a good life is not giving a fuck about more; it's giving a fuck about less, giving a fuck about only what is true and immediate and important.

Our society today, through the wonders of consumer culture and hey-look-my-life-is-cooler-than-yours social media, has bred a whole generation of people who believe that having negative experiences - anxiety, fear, guilt, etc... - is totally not okay.

The desire of more positive experience is itself a negative experience. And, paradoxically, the acceptance of one's negative experience is itself a positive experience. (my note: really similar to what said Buddha).
"You will never be happy if you continue to search for what happiness consists of. You will never live if you are looking for the meaning of life."

Any attempt to escape the negative, to avoid it or quash it or silence it, only backfires. The avoidance of suffering is a form of suffering. The avoidance of struggle is struggle. The denial of failure is a failure. Hiding what is shameful is itself a form of shame.
You must give a fuck about something. But what do we give a fuck about?
When a person has no problems, the mind automatically finds a way to invent some.

Today people no longer realize it's okay for things to suck sometimes. Some suffering is always inevitable - no matter what you do, life is comprised of failures, loss, regrets, and even death. We should let go of trying to resist them.

We suffer because is biologically useful. It is nature's preferred agent for inspiring change. We are wired to become dissatisfied with whatever we have and satisfied by only what we do not have. Own own pain an misery aren't a bug of human evolution; they're a feature.
Happiness comes from solving problems. The secret sauce is in the solving problems, not in not having them in the first place. Happiness is a for of action; it's an activity.
Negative emotions are a call to action. When you feel them, it's because you're supposed to do something.
Emotions never last. Whatever makes us happy today will no longer make us happy tomorrow. A fixation on happiness inevitably amounts to a never-ending pursuit of "something else".
"What pain do you want in your life? What are you willing to struggle for?"

I thought I wanted something but it turns out I didn't. End of story. I wanted the reward and not the struggle. I wanted the result and not the process. I was in love with not the fight but only the victory. And life doesn't work that way.
We are not all exceptional.

The true measurement of self-worth is how a person feels about her negative experiences. A person who actually has a high self-worth is able to look at negative parts of his character frankly and acts to improve them.

If we have problems that are unsolvable, our conscious figures that we're either uniquely special or uniquely defective in some way. We become entitled. This entitlement plays out in one of two ways: I'm awesome and the rest of you all suck, or I suck and the rest of you are all awesome. In both cases I deserve a special treatment.
Construing everything in life as to make yourself out to be constantly victimized requires just as much selfishness as the opposite.

There's no such thing as a personal problem. If you've got a problem, chances are millions of other people have had it in the past, have it now, and are going to have it in the future. It just means that you're not special.
That flood of extreme information from news has conditioned us to believe that exceptionalism is the new normal.
We are all destined to do something truly extraordinary. We all deserve greatness.

You should accept truths of life: "Your actions actually don't matter that much in the grand scheme of things" and "The vast majority of your life will be boring and not noteworthy, and that's okay.". In this way the constant pressure to be something amazing, to be the next big thing, will be lifted off your back. The stress and anxiety of always feeling inadequate and constantly needing to prove yourself will dissipate. And the knowledge and acceptance of your own mundane existence will actually free you to accomplish what you truly wish to accomplish, without judgement or lofty expectations. You will have a growing appreciation for life's basic experiences: the pleasures of simple friendship, creating something, helping a person in need, reading a good book, laughing with someone you care about. Sounds boring, doesn't it? That's because these things are ordinary. But maybe the're ordinary for a reason: because they are what actually matters.
If your suffering mean something, you'll be able to endure it, or perhaps even enjoy it.

There are multiple layers to self-awareness. The first layer is simple understanding of one's emotions. The second layer is ability to ask why we feel certain emotions. The third layer is personal values: why do I consider this to be a success/failure? How am I choosing to measure myself? By what standard am I judging myself and everyone around me? Our values determine the metrics by which we measure ourselves and everyone else.
Shitty values:
Pleasure: is not the cause of happiness; rather, it is the effect. If you get the other stuff right, then pleasure will naturally occur as a byproduct.
Material success: research shows that one one is able to provide for basic physical needs, the correlation between happiness and worldly success quickly approaches zero.

Always being right: it is far more helpful to assume that you're ignorant and don't know a whole lot. This keeps you unattached to superstitious or poorly informed beliefs and promotes a constant state of learning and growth.

Staying positive: sometimes life sucks, and the healthiest thing you can do is admit it. Denying negative emotions leads experiencing deeper and more prolonged negative emotions and to emotional dysfunctions. Constant positivity is a form of avoidance, not a valid solution to life's problems.
Good values are: reality-based, socially constructive, immediate and controllable. Bad values are the opposite.
Good, healthy values are achieved internally. Bad values are generally reliant on external events.
Self improvement is really about prioritizing better values.
Five counterintuitive values: taking responsibility, acknowledging uncertainty, willingness to fail, acceptance of rejection and contemplation of mortality.
Taking responsibility:
We are responsible for everything in our lives, no matter the external circumstances. We always control how we interpret what happens to us, as well as how we respond.
Accepting responsibility for our problems is the first step to solving them.

A lot of people hesitate to take responsibility for their problems because they believe that to be responsible for your problems is to also be at fault for your problems. But fault is past tense. Responsibility is present tense. Fault results from choices that have already been made. Responsibility results from choices you're currently making, every second of every day.

While she was to blame for how I felt, she was not responsible for how I felt. I was. I took on the responsibility of striving to make my future relationship with women that much better. My ex leaving me, while one of the most painful experiences I've ever had, was also one of the most important and influential experiences of my life. I credit it with inspiring a significant amount of personal growth. I learned more from that single problem than dozens of my successes combined.
Pain is inevitable for all of us, but we got to choose what it means to and for us.

The "Victimhood chic" makes anyone who is offended by anything feels as though they're being oppressed in some way and therefore deserve to be outraged and to have a certain amount of attention. The biggest problem is that it sucks attention away from actual victims.
Change is as simple as choosing to give a fuck about something else. It really is that simple. It's just not easy.
Acknowledging uncertainty:
I thought that love was something that just happened, not something you worked for.

Just as Present you can look back on Past you's every flaw and mistake, Future you will look back on Present you's assumptions and notice similar flaws. And that will be good thing, because that will mean I have grown.

It's easier to sit in a painful certainty that nobody would find you attractive, that nobody appreciates your talents, than to actually test those beliefs and find out for sure. These beliefs are designed to give us moderate comfort now by mortgaging grater happiness late.
Certainty is the enemy of growth. Being wrong opens up to the possibility of change. Being wrong brings the opportunity of growth.

We don't actually know what a positive and a negative experience is. Some of the most difficult and stressful moments of our lives also end up being the most formative and motivating. Some of the best and most gratifying experiences of our lives are also the most distracting and demotivating. Don't trust your conception of positive/negative experiences. All that we know for certain is what hurts in the moment and what doesn't. And that's not worth much.
Brain is imperfect: we mistake things we see and hear and once we create meaning for ourselves, our brains are designed to hold on to that meaning.

The more you try to be certain about something, the more uncertain and insecure you will feel. The more you embrace being uncertain and not knowing, the more comfortable you will feel in knowing what you don't know.
Famous laws:
"Works expand so as to fill up the time available for its completion". Parkinson's law.
"Whatever can go wrong will go wrong". Murphy's law.
"The more something threatens your identity, the more you will avoid it". Manson's law. (New)

The Buddhism argues that your idea of who "you" are is an arbitrary mental construction and that you should let go of the idea that "you" exist at all; that the arbitrary metrics by which you define yourself actually trap you, and thus you're better off letting go of everything.
As a general rule, we're all the world's worst observers of ourselves. When we're angry, or jealous, or upset, we're oftentimes the last ones to figure it out.

Question to breed a little more uncertainty in your life: "What if I'm wrong?", "What would it mean if I were wrong?", "Would being wrong create a better or a worse problem than my current problem, for both myself and others?"

If it's down to me being screwed up, or everybody else being screwed up, its far, far, far more likely that I'm the one who's screwed up. If it feels like it's you versus the world, chances are it's really just you versus yourself.
Willingness to fail:
If someone is better than you at something, then it's likely because she has failed at it more than you have.

Fear and anxiety and sadness are not necessarily always undesirable or unhelpful states of mind; rather, they are often representative of the necessary pain of psychological growth. And to deny that pain is to deny our own potential. Just as one suffer physical pain to build stronger bone and muscle, one must suffer physical pain to develop greater emotional resilience, a stronger sense of self, increased compassion, and generally happier life.

Our most radical changes in perspective often happen at the tail end of our worst moments. It's only when we feel intense pain that we're willing to look at our values and question why they seem to be failing us. We need some sort of existential crisis to take an objective look at how we've been deriving meaning in our life, and then consider changing course. Pain is part of the process. It's important to feel it.

If you're stuck on a problem, don't sit there and think about it; just start working on it. Even if you don't know what you're doing, the simple act of working on it will eventually cause the right ideas to show up in your head. Actions isn't just the effect of motivation; it's also the cause of it.
Acceptance of rejection:
The only way to achieve meaning and a sense of importance in ones life is through a rejection of alternatives, a narrowing of freedom, a choice of commitment to one place, one belief, or one person.
There is such a pressure in the West to be likable that people often reconfigure their entire personality depending on the person they're dealing with.
To value something, we must reject what is not that something. To value X, we must reject non-X.
Honesty is a natural human craving. But part of having honesty in our lives is becoming comfortable with saying and hearing the word "no".
Shakespeare wrote "Romeo and Juliet" not to celebrate romance, but rather to satirize it, to show how absolutely nutty it was.

There are healthy forms of love and unhealthy forms of love. Unhealthy love is based on two people trying to escape their problems through their emotions for each other. Healthy love is based on two people acknowledging and addressing their own problems with each other's support. People in a healthy relationship with strong boundaries will take responsibility for their own values and problems and not take responsibility for their partner's values and problems.

An overbearing mother take responsibility for every problem in her children's lives. Her own entitlement then encourages an entitlement in her children, as they grown up to believe other people should always be responsible for their problems.
You (in a relationship) both should support each other. But only because you choose to support and e supported. Not because you feel obligated or entitled.
Litmus test: ask yourself, "If I refuse, how would the relationship change?" Similarly, ask, "If my partner refused something I wanted, how would the relationship change?"
The last person I should ever have to censor myself with is the woman I love.
You don't feel loved until you trust that the love being expressed towards you comes without any special conditions or baggage attached to it.
What needs to happen is that cheaters have to start peeling away at their self-awareness onion and figure out what fucked-up values caused them to break the trust of the relationship.

When trust is destroyed, it can be rebuild only if the following two steps happen: 1) the trust-breaker admits the true values that caused the breach and owns up to them, and 2) the trust-breaker builds a solid track record of improved behavior over time. Without first step, there should be no attempt at reconciliation in the first place.
Commitment, in its own way, offers a wealth of opportunity and experiences that would otherwise never be available to me, no matter where I went or what I did.
Commitment makes decision-making easier and removes any fear of missing out; knowing that what you already have is good enough, why would you ever stress about chasing more, more, more again?

Breadth of experience is likely necessary and desirable when you're young, you have to go out there and discover that seems worth investing yourself in. But depth is where the gold is buried. And you have to stay committed to something and go deep to dig it up.
"Seek the truth for yourself, and I will meet you there!"
Death is the light by which the shadow of all of life's meaning is measured.
The book "The Denial of Death" makes two point:

Humans are unique in that we're the only animals that can conceptualize and think about ourselves abstractly. Because we're able to conceptualize alternate version of reality, we are also the only animal capable of imagining a reality without ourselves in it. This realization causes a deep existential anxiety that underlies everything we think or do.

We have two "selves". Th physical self and the conceptual self. We are all aware on some level that our physical self will eventually die, but we try to construct a conceptual self that will live forever. Our "immortality project". All the meaning in our life is shaped by this innate desire to never truly die.

People's immortality projects are actually the problems, not the solution; rather than attempting to implement their conceptual self across the world, people should question their conceptual self and become more comfortable with the reality of their own death. This is the "bitter antidote": while death is bad, it is inevitable. We should not avoid this realization, but rather come to terms with it as best as we can. Once we become comfortable with the fact of our own death we can then choose our values more freely, unrestrained by the illogical quest of immortality.
"The fear of death follows the fear of life. A man who lives fully is prepared to die at any time".

Confronting the reality of our own mortality is important because it obliterates all the crappy, fragile, superficial values in life. Death confronts all of us with a far more painful and important question: What is our legacy? We avoid thinking about it. One because it's hard, two because it's scary, three because we have no fucking clue what we're doing.

Without acknowledging the ever-present gaze of death, the superficial will appear important, and the important will appear superficial. Happiness comes from the same thing: caring about something greater than yourself, believing that you are a contributing component is some much larger entity. And entitlement strips this away from us.

The pampering of the modern mind has resulted in a population that feels deserving of something without earning that something, a population that feels they have a right to something without sacrificing for it. Our culture today confuses great attention and great success, assuming them to be the same thing. But they are not. You are great. Already. Whether you realize it or not. Whether everybody else realizes it or not. You're already great because in the face of endless confusion and certain death, you continue to choose what to give a fuck about and what not to. This simple optioning for your own values in life, already makes you beautiful, already makes you successful, and already makes you loved.
There is nothing to be afraid of. Ever.

This acceptance of my death has made everything easier - untangling my addictions, identifying and confronting my own entitlement, accepting responsibility for my own problems - suffering through my fears and uncertainties, accepting my failures and embracing my rejections.

Calculate or get the baseline prediction (the average over the last timesteps or over similar variables in the last timestep)
With no evidence, you stick with the baseline. If you're completely sure, you stay with the intuitive prediction.
In other cases (almost all cases), start from the baseline and move towards the intuitive percentage based on how sure you feel or how strong is the correlation between the two.
While you do so think carefully about how much you know.
Algorithm > Intuition (a little of anchoring too).
How to take a decision about a person:
Select few traits that are prerequisite for the success in the on which she's assessed (should be max 6 and as independent as possible).
Make a list of factual questions to assess the reliability of the trait and think how to score the answers.
Ask every question collecting all infos about one trait, assessing it and then continuing with the other trait.
At the end, sum the result of each trait (or calculate a weighted sum) and choose the one that scored best. (My Idea: the score to evaluate should be the logaritmic of the actual result scored)
Don't rely on intuitions.
Intuition in experts is nothing more than recognition.
How to know if intuition is likely to be correct:
An intuition is likely to be correct if all these are true:
- The environment is sufficiently regular.
- The regularities are learnt through prolonged practice.
- The feedback is relatively fast.
The "inside view" is the case in exam. The "outside view" are all the other similar cases, that shouldn't be ignored.
How to predict costs and time for a plan:
Avoid plan unrealistically close to best-case scenario.
Identify a reference class for your plan.
Obtain statistics of the reference class and use them to generate a baseline.
Use the infos about specific case to adjust the baseline prediction.
Why are we optimistic? We anchor to our plan, neglect the skills of the others, neglect the role of luck and neglect what we don't know.
How to take decisions less optimistically:
Come to a decision, but not commit it.
Ask to people that know everything about the decision: "Imagine we are in the future and the plan we are implementing is a disaster. Take 5 to 10 minutes to write a brief history of what happened"
Re-evaluate the decision accounting also for these worst-case scenario.
Regret is an emotion that you'll feel more if you actively couse it going far from standard.
How to avoid regret:
Anticipate regret, consider its possibility and write it down.
Preclude the hindsight fallacy being either very thorough or completely casual when making decision.

Even though you read much Zen literature, you must read each sentence with a fresh mind. You should not say, "I know what Zen is", or "I have attained enlightenment".
