Right practice
Zazen posture. The position express the oneness of duality: not two, not one. Our body and mind are both two and one.

Keep your spine straight. Pull your chin in, when your chin is tilted up, you are probably dreaming. Press your diaphragm down towards your lower abdomen. Put your left hand on top of your right, touch your thumbs lightly together.
When you try to attain something, your mind starts to wander about something else. When you do not try to attain anything, you have your own body and mind right here.
Usually we try to change something other than ourselves. It is impossible to organize things if you yourself are not in order.
Try always to keep the right posture, not only when you practice zazen, but in all your activities.
Buddha was not interested in some metaphysical existence, but in his own body and mind, here and now. Everything that exists has Buddha nature, that was his enlightenment.
When we practice zazen our mind is always following our breathing. What we call "I" is just a swinging door which moves when we inhale and when we exhale.
"I" means to be aware of the universe in the form of I.
All that we should do is just do something as it comes. Do something! Whatever it is, we should do it, even if it is not-doing something. We should live in this moment.
When we lose our balance we die, but at the same time we also develop ourselves, we grow.
Ancient painters used to practice putting dots on a paper in artistic disorder. this is rather difficult. Usually what we do is arranged in some order.
If you want to obtain perfect calmness in your zazen, you should not be bothered by the various images you find in your mind. Let them come, and let them go. Then they will be under control.

If you try to calm your mind the effort that will help you is to count your breathing, or to concentrate on your inhaling and exhaling. But to concentrate your mind is not the true purpose of Zen. The true purpose is to see things as they are, to observe things as they are, and to let everything go as it goes.
As long as you have rules, you have a chance for freedom.

When you are practicing zazen, do not try to stop your thinking. Let it stop by itself. If something comes into your mind, let it come, and let it go out. It will not stay long. When you try to stop your thinking, it means you are bothered by it. Do not be bothered by anything.

Nothing comes from outside your mind. Nothing outside yourself can cause any trouble. You yourself make the waves in your mind. If you leave your mind as it is, it will become calm. This mind is called big mind.
As your mind does not expect anything from outside, it is always filled.
With big mind we accept each of our experiences as if recognizing the face we see in a mirror as our own.

Any effort we make is not good for our practice because it creates waves in our mind. It is impossible, however, to attain absolute calmness of our mind without any effort. We must take some effort, but we must forget ourselves in the effort we make.
In zazen posture, your mind and body have great power to accept things as they are, whether agreeable or disagreeable.
Even though you cannot take the right posture, when you arouse you real, way-seeking mind, you can practice Zen in its true sense.

To stop your mind does not mean to stop the activities of mind. It means your mind pervades your whole body. Your mind follows you breathing. With your whole mind you sit with painful legs without being disturbed by them.
As long as you are concerned about what you do, that is dualistic. If you're not concerned about what you do, you will not say so. When you sit, you will sit. When you eat, you will eat. That is all.
In your big mind, everything has the same values. Everything is Buddha himself. In your practice you should accept everything as it is, giving to each thing the same respect given to a Buddha.

We can say either that we make progress little by little, or that we do not even expect to make progress. Just to be sincere and make our full effort in each moment is enough. There is no Nirvana outside our practice.
For human beings there is no other practice than this practice. There is no other way of life that this way of life.
In zazen what you're doing is not for sake of anything. You may feel as if you are doing something special, but actually it is only the expression of your true nature.
Do not thing about anything. Just remain on your cushion without expecting anything. Then eventually you will resume your own true nature.
Right attitude
Our way is not to sit to acquire something; it is to express our true nature. That is our practice.
Just appreciate the view from the train. That is our way. There is no need for passengers to be curious about the track. Someone will take care of it.
In the midst of noise and change, your mind will be quiet and stable.
Our unexciting way of practice may appear to be very negative. This is not so. It is a wise and effective way to work on ourselves. It is just very plain.

Our effort in our practice should be directed from achievement to non-achievement. If you think you will get something from practicing zazen, already you are involved in impure practice. You should not be tainted by it. When you practice zazen, just practice zazen. If enlightenment comes, it just comes. We should not attach to the attainment.
If you try to see the quality of zazen, you have no quality.
When you do something, you should do it with your whole body and mind. You should burn yourself completely.
Even though we are sleepy, and we are tired of practicing zazen, of repeating the same thing day after day; even so, we continue our practice.
You become discouraged with your practice when your practice has been idealistic. You have some gaining idea in your practice, and it is not pure enough.
Do not think you will necessary be aware of your own enlightenment.
Another mistake will be to practice for the sake of the joy you find in it. When your practice is involved in a feeling of joy, it is not in very good shape either.

Do not give up your practice; continue it, knowing your weakness. Your practice cannot be perfect, but without being discouraged by this, you should continue it. This is the secret of practice. Here there is no gaining idea.
When someone believes in a particular religion, his attitude becomes more and more a sharp angle pointing away from himself. In our way the point of the angle is always towards ourselves.
The purpose of studying Buddhism is not to study Buddhism, but to study ourselves.

Teaching disciples has four way: sometimes you should talk about the disciple itself, sometimes you should talk about the teaching itself, sometimes you should give an interpretation of the disciple or the teaching, sometimes you should not give any instruction at all to your disciple.
To study Buddhism is to study of ourselves. To study of ourselves is to forget ourselves.
When you are you, that is zazen.

When you are in the present moment, then there is no problem. When you start to wander about in some delusion which is something apart from you yourself, then your surroundings are not real anymore, and your mind is not real anymore.
When you are you, you see thing as they are, and you become one with your surroundings. There is your true self.
Cultivate your spirit means not to go seeking for something outside yourself.
Our understanding of Buddhism should not be just gathering many pieces of information, seeking to gain knowledge. Instead of gathering knowledge, you should clear your mind.
When you listen to someone, you should give up all your preconceived ideas and your subjective opinions; you should just listen to him, just observe what his way is.
True communication depends upon our being straightforward with one another. Zen masters are very straightforward.
The more you understand our thinking, the more you find it difficult to talk about. Our way is not something to talk about, but something to practice.

When you say something to someone, he might not accept it, but do not try to make him understand it intellectually. Do not argue with him; just listen to his objections until he himself finds something wrong with them.
Big mind is something to express, but it is not something to figure out. Big mind is something you have, not something to seek for.

Before we were born we had no feeling, we were one with the universe. After we are separated by birth from this oneness, as the water falling from the waterfall is separated by the wind and rocks, then we have feeling. You attach to the feeling you have without knowing just how this kind of feeling is created. Whether it is separated into drops or not, water is water. Our life and death are the same thing. When we realize this fact we have no fear of death anymore, and we have no actual difficulty in our life. How very glad the water must be to come back to the original river! For us, just now, we have some fear of death, but after we resume our true original nature, there is Nirvana. When you realize this fact, you will discover how meaningless your old interpretation was. You will find the true meaning of life, and even though you have difficulty falling upright from the top of the waterfall to the bottom of the mountain. you will enjoy your life.
Right understanding
Zen is not concerned about philosophical understanding. We emphasize practice.

Human nature is without ego. When we have no idea of ego, we have Buddha's view of life. Our egoistic ideas are delusion, covering Buddha's view of life. We are always creating and following them, and in repeating this process over and over again, our life becomes completely occupied by ego-centered idea. This is called karmic life, or karma.
We have to make our effort in this moment.
When we realize the everlasting truth of "everything changes" and find our composure in it, we find ourselves in Nirvana. The cause of suffering is our non-acceptance of this truth.

We should find the truth in this world, through our difficulties, through our suffering. Pleasure is not different from difficulty. Good is not different from bad. Bad is good; good is bad. They are two sides of one coin. So enlightenment should be in practice.

When you do something, if you fix your mind on the activity with some confidence, the quality of your state of mind is the activity itself. When you are concentrated on the quality of your being, you are prepared for the activity.
When I am sitting, there is no other person, but this does not mean I ignore you. I am completely one with every existence in the phenomenal world. So when I sit, you sit; everything sits with me.
The true practice of zazen is to sit as if drinking water when you are thirsty. There you have naturalness.
If you want to understand Buddhism, you must give up the idea of substantiality or existence. The bird both exists and not exists at the same time.

Concentration means freedom. Your effort should be directed at nothing. You should be concentrated on nothing. In zazen practice we say your mind should be concentrated on your breathing, but the way you keep your mind on your breathing is to forget all about yourself and just sit and feel your breathing.
When we realize that everything we see is a part of emptiness, we can have no attachment to any existence; we realize that everything is just a tentative form and color.
Even before we practice, enlightenment is there.
Just to see, and to be ready to see things with your whole mind, is zazen practice. If we are prepared for thinking, there is no need to make an effort to think. This is called mindfulness.

Wisdom is something which will come out of your mindfulness. So the point is to be ready for observing things, and to be ready for thinking. This is called emptiness of your mind. Emptiness is nothing but the practice of zazen.
No matter what god or doctrine you believe in, if you become attached to it, your belief will be based more or less on a self-centered idea.

When the Buddha nature is personified we call it Buddha; when we understand it as the ultimate truth we call it Dharma; and when we accept the truth and act as a part of the Buddha, we call ourselves Sangha.

Now it is raining, but we don't know what will happen in the next moment. By the time we go out it might be a beautiful day, or a stormy day. Since we don't know, let's appreciate the sound of the rain now.

There is no difference between the foolish man and the wise man. It is so. But if I say this people may think that I am emphasizing oneness. That is not so. We do not emphasize anything. All we want ti do is to know things as just as they are.
The trying to do something in itself is enlightenment.

Which is more important: to attain enlightenment or to attain enlightenment before you attain enlightenment; to make a million dollars, or to enjoy you life in your effort, little by little, even though it is impossible to make that million; to be successful, or to find some meaning in your effort to be successful?

Zazen practice is the practice in which we resume our pure way of life, beyond any gaining idea, and beyond fame and profit. There is no need to intellectualize about what our pure original nature is, because it is beyond our intellectual understanding. And there is no need to appreciate it, because it is beyond our appreciation. So just sit, without any idea of gain, and with the purest intention, to remain as quiet as our original nature. For us there is no need to understand what Zen is. We are practicing zazen. We do not even know what we are doing when we just practice with a pure mind.
(Written by me) I don't know what Buddhism is. But I know what to do to practice. I practice zazen everyday.
Buddhism is not some particular teaching. Buddhism is just Truth, which includes various truths in it.
If you find a delusion and try to expel it it will only persist the more. Just say "Oh, this is just delusion", and not be bothered by it.
You should not propagate our way by wonderful philosophical thoughts. If you want to be a sincere Buddhist, the best way is to sit.
Epilogue

You should be able to appreciate things as an expression of big mind. This is more than faith. This is the ultimate truth which you cannot reject. Whether it is difficult or easy to practice, difficult or easy to understand, you can only practice it. If you have this confidence in your big mind, you are already a Buddhist in the true sense, even though you do not attain enlightenment.
If you think that big mind is somewhere outside yourself, outside of your practice, then that is a mistake. Everyone has Buddha nature.

We must have beginner's mind, free from possessing anything, a mind that knows everything is in flowing change. Nothing exists but momentarily in its present form and color. One thing flows into another and cannot be grasped.
Afterwords
Suzuki has confidence that you, whoever you are, can understand en, Buddhism, reality, truth, yourself.

Zero to One notes
Important ideas:
Preface
If you're copying founders, you're not learning from them. It's easier to copy a model than to make something new.
Successful people find value in unexpected places, and they do this by thinking about business from first principles instead of formulas.
Chapter 1 - The challenge of the future
Interview question: "What important truth do very few people agree with you on?"
Going from 0 to 1, or progressing vertically, is harder to imagine because it requires doing something nobody else has ever done.
The word for horizontal progress, or copying things that work, is globalization. The word for vertical progress, or doing new things, is technology.
Most people think the future of the world will be defined by globalization, but the truth is that technology matters more. Globalization without technology is unsustainable.
Chapter 2 - Party like it's 1999
Conventional beliefs only ever come to appear arbitrary and wrong in retrospect.
(Wrong) beliefs that are become a dogma in the startup world:
Make incremental advances.
Stay lean and flexible.
Improve on the competition.
Focus on product, not sales.
The opposite principles are probably more correct:
Is better risk boldness than triviality.
A bad plan is better than no plan.
Competitive markets destroy profits.
Sales matters just as much as product.
Chapter 3 - All happy companies are different
Ask yourself: "what valuable company is nobody building?".

There are two types of model for companies: perfect competition and monopoly. Under perfect competition, in the long run no company makes an economic profit. If you want to create and capture lasting value, don't build an undifferentiated commodity business.

Both monopolists and non-monopolists lies to seem less extreme. Monopolists lie to protect themselves, bragging about their great monopoly invites being audited, scrutinized and attacked. Non-monopolists tell the opposite lie defining your market extremely narrowly so that you dominate it by definition. But if you lose sight of competitive reality and focus on trivial differentiation factors, your business is unlikely to survive.
The competitive ecosystem pushes people toward ruthlessness or death.

Monopolies deserve their bad reputation, but only in a world where nothing changes. Monopolies can keep innovating because profit enable them to make the long-term plans and to finance the ambitious research projects that firms locked in competition can't dream of.
In business, equilibrium means stasis, and stasis means death. Monopoly is the condition of every successful business.
Chapter 4 - The ideology of competition

Higher education is the place where people who had big plans in high school get stuck in rivalries with equally smart peers over conventional careers like management consulting and investment banking,
Winning is better than losing, but everybody loses when the war isn't one worth fighting.

If you can't beat a rival, it may be better merge. But sometimes you have to fight and when that's true, you should fight to win. There is no middle ground: either don't throw any punches, or strike hard and end it quickly.
Chapter 5 - Last mover advantage
A great business is defined by its ability to generate cash flow in the future.

For a company to be valuable it must grow and endure, if you focus on near-term growth above all else, you miss the most important question you should be asking: will this business still be around a decade from now?
The most important characteristics that a monopoly should have to be such, are:

Proprietary technology is the most substantive advantage a company can have because it makes your product difficult or impossible to replicate. This technology should be at least 10 times better than its closest substitute in some important dimension.

Network effect make a product more useful if more people use it. That can be very powerful, but you'll never reap them unless your product is valuable to its very first users when the network is necessary small.
Economy of scale. A monopoly business gets stronger as it gets bigger. A good startup should have the potential for great scale built into its first design.
Branding. Creating a strong brand is a powerful way to claim a monopoly.
Every startup should start with a very small market. The perfect target is a small group of particular people concentrated together and served by few or no competitors.
Once you create and dominate a niche market, then you should gradually expand into related and slightly broader markets. You shouldn't try to disrupt something, avoid competition as much as possible.
Is good to be the fist mover, but it's better to be the last mover.
Chapter 6 - You are not a lottery ticket
Statistics doesn't work when the sample size is one.
There are 4 different types of approach:
An indefinite pessimist looks out onto a bleak future, but he has no idea what to do about it.
A definite pessimist believes the future can be unknown, but since it will bleak, he must prepare for it.
To a definite optimist, the future will be better than the present if he plans and works to make it better.
To an indefinite optimist, the future will be better, but he doesn't know how exactly, so he won't make any specific plans.

Why should you expect your business to succeed without a plan to make it happen? You can change the world through careful planning, not by listening to focus group feedback or copying others' successes.
A business with a good definite plan will always be underrated in a world where people see the future as random. We have to find our way back to a definite future. You are not a lottery ticket.
Chapter 7 - Follow the money
We don't live in a normal world, we live under a power law.

The biggest secret in venture capital is that the best investment in a successful fund equals or outperforms the entire rest of the fund combined. Every single company in a good venture portfolio must have the potential to succeed at vast scale.
Chapter 8 - Secrets
If there are many secrets left in the world, there are probably many world-changing companies yet to be started.

Most people act as if there were no secrets left to find. Why has so much of our society come to believe that there are no hard secrets left? It might start with geography. There are no blank spaces left on the map anymore. Along with that, four social trends have conspired to root out belief in secrets.
Incrementalism: they taught us that the right way to do thing is to proceed one very small step at a time.
Risk aversion: people are scared of secrets because they are scared of being wrong.
Complacency: why search for a new secret if you can comfortably collect rents on everything that has already been done?
Flatness: as globalization advances, people perceive the world as one homogeneous, highly competitive marketplace.

If you don't believe in secrets you'd have to believe we've already solved all great questions. To say that there are no secrets left today would mean that we live in a society with no hidden injustices.
You can't find secrets without looking for them. If you think something hard is impossible, you'll never even start trying to achieve it.
There are two type of secrets: secrets of nature and secrets about people.
The best place to look for secrets is where no one else is looking.
Who do you tell a secret? Whoever you need to, and no more. A great company is a conspiracy to change the world; when you share your secret, the recipient becomes a fellow conspirator.
Chapter 9 - Foundations
A startup messed up at its foundation cannot be fixed.
Founders should share a prehistory before they start a company together, otherwise they're just rolling dice.

In the boardroom, less is more. The smaller the board, the easier it is for the directors to communicate, to reach consensus, and to exercise effective oversight. A board of three is ideal, your board should never exceed five people, unless your company is publicly held.

A company does better the less it pays the CEO. Low CEO pay sets standard for everyone else. But you can offer something that's far better than money: part ownership of the company itself. It's the perfect way to keep everyone in the company broadly aligned.
Chapter 10 - The mechanics of mafia
No company has a culture, every company is a culture.

Stronger relationships make us not just happier and better at work but also more successful in our careers even beyond the first company. It's a good idea to hire people who would actually enjoy working together.

General and undifferentiated pitches don't say anything about why a recruit should join your company instead of many others. There are two general kinds of answers: answers about your mission and answers about your team.
Don't fight the perk war. Anybody who would be more powerfully swayed by some unimportant benefit would be a bad addition to your team.
From the outside, everyone in your company should be different in the same way. Startups should make their early staff as personally similar as possible.
On the inside, every individual should be sharply distinguished by her work. Make every person in the company responsible for doing just one thing.
People at a successful startup are fanatically right about something those outside it have missed.
Chapter 11 - If you build it, will they come?
Customers will not come just because you build it. You have to make that happen, and it's harder than it looks.

Advertising matters because it works. It works on nerds, and it works on you. It doesn't exists to make you buy a product right away; it exists to embed subtle impressions that will drive sales later.
It takes hard work to make sales look easy.
All salesman are actors: their priority is persuasion, not sincerity. Like acting, sales works best when hidden.
It's better to think of distribution as something essential to the design of your product.
Superior sales and distribution by itself can create a monopoly, even with no product differentiation. The converse is not true.
In between personal sales and traditional advertising there is a dead zone.
Advertising can work for startups too, but only when your customer acquisition costs and customer lifetime value make every other distribution channel uneconomical.
A product is viral if its core functionality encourages users to invite their friends to become users too.
If you can get just one distribution channel to work, you have a great business. If you try for several but don't nail one, you're finished.
Remember also that you must also sell your company to employees and investors.
Chapter 12 - Man and machine
The most valuable business of coming decades will be built by entrepreneurs who seek to empower people rather than try to make them obsolete.
Computers are tools, not rivals. Properly understood, technology is the one way for us to escape competition in a globalizing world.

We're impressed with small feats accomplished by computers alone, but we ignore big achievements from t complementarity between humans and machines because the human contributions makes them less uncanny.
The most valuable companies in the future won't ask what problems can be solved with computers alone. Instead, they'll ask: how can computers help humans solve hard problems?
As we find new ways to use computers, they won't just get better at the kinds of things people already do; they'll help us to do what was previously unimaginable.
Chapter 13 - Seeing green
Every business must answer to those questions:
The engineering question: can you create breakthrough technology instead of incremental improvements?
A great technology company should have proprietary technology an order of magnitude better than its nearest substitute.
The timing question: is now the right time to start your particular business?
Entering a small moving market can be a good strategy, but only is you have a definite and realistic plan to take it over.
The monopoly question: are you starting with a big share of a small market?
If you can't monopolize a unique solution for a small market, you'll be stuck with a vicious competition.
The people question: do you have the right team?
There's nothing wrong with a CEO who can sell, but if he actually looks like a salesman, he's probably bad at sales and worse at tech.
The distribution question: do you have a way to not just create but deliver your product?
Selling and delivering product is at least as important as the product itself.
The durability question: will your market position be defensible 10 and 20 years intro the future?
What will the world look like 10 and 20 years from now, and how will my business fit in? What will prevent other companies from wiping out my business?
The secret question: have you identified a unique opportunity that others don't see?

If something is socially good, is it for society, or merely seen good by society? Progress isn't held back by some difference between corporate greed and nonprofit goodness; instead, we're held back by the sameness of both.
Doing something different is what's truly good for society, and it's also what allows a business to profit by monopolizing a new market.
Chapter 14 - The founder's paradox
So many founders seem to have extreme traits. When you plot the out, founders' traits appear to follow an inverse normal distribution.
These traits could be present from birth (nature) or acquired from an individual's environment (nurture).

The lesson for business is that we need founders. The lesson for founders is that individual prominence and adulation can never be enjoyed except on the condition that it might be exchanged for individual notoriety and demonization at any moment.

Don't overestimate your own power as an individual. The single greatest danger for a founder is to become so certain of his own myth that he loses his mind. But an equally insidious danger for every business is to lose all sense of myths and mistake disenchantment for wisdom.
Conclusion: stagnation or singularity

Our task today is to find singular ways to create the new things that will make the future not just different, but better - to go from 0 to 1. The essential first step is to think for yourself. Only by seeing our world anew, as fresh and strange as it was to ancients who saw it first, can we both re-create it and preserve it for the future.
